title: Diagnosing Susac Syndrome Despite Incomplete Clinical Triad: A Case Report of Convergent Atypical Neuroimaging and Inflammatory Cerebrospinal Fluid Findings: Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Susac syndrome (SuS) is a rare autoimmune endotheliopathy involving the brain, retina, and inner ear. Because patients frequently present without the complete clinical triad of encephalopathy, branch retinal artery occlusions (BRAO), and sensorineural hearing loss (SNHL), diagnosis can be challenging. The European Susac Consortium (EuSaC) criteria classify SuS according to objective involvement of the brain, retinal, and vestibulocochlear domains; however, many patients do not fulfill criteria for probable or definite disease at initial presentation. Furthermore, neuroimaging and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) findings may overlap with inflammatory demyelinating disorders such as multiple sclerosis (MS). We report a case where EuSaC criteria was not met, however there was strong clinical and radiographic evidence to support the diagnosis of SuS. This case brings to question whether strict fulfillment of EuSaC criteria is needed to initiate early inpatient treatment to prevent irreversible neurological deficits. Case presentation We report the case of a woman in her early forties with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, chronic kidney disease, recurrent ischemic strokes, and an unspecified hypercoagulable disorder who presented with progressive gait instability, dizziness, and bilateral lower extremity weakness. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) demonstrated characteristic central corpus callosum “snowball” lesions and cerebellar leptomeningeal enhancement. CSF analysis revealed elevated immunoglobulin G (IgG) index, elevated IgG synthesis rate, and markedly elevated myelin basic protein (MBP) in the absence of oligoclonal bands (OCB). At the time of presentation, only the brain domain of the EuSaC criteria was objectively fulfilled, and the patient therefore did not meet criteria for probable or definite SuS. Nevertheless, the characteristic neuroimaging phenotype, inflammatory CSF profile without oligoclonal bands, and absence of typical MS features strongly favored SuS and prompted treatment with high dose steroids and further diagnostic evaluation. Conclusions This case demonstrates that strict fulfillment of EuSaC criteria may not be required to recognize SuS when characteristic neuroradiographic findings and supportive clinical features are present. Recognition of central corpus callosum “snowball” lesions and cerebellar leptomeningeal enhancement may facilitate earlier diagnosis and treatment, potentially reducing irreversible neurologic, retinal, and auditory morbidity.

title: A Dangerous Evolution of Retroperitoneal Infection to Infrarenal Abdominal Aortic Pseudoaneurysm: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the infrarenal abdominal aorta is a rare and potentially fatal complication of infection. Early diagnosis can be challenging because clinical symptoms are often nonspecific, and initial imaging may demonstrate only inflammatory changes without aneurysmal formation. This case highlights the importance of recognizing evolving radiographic findings in patients with a history of recurrent infection. Case presentation A 46-year-old man with a history of recurrent pelvic abscesses secondary to diverticulitis presented with three days of back pain, nausea, and vomiting. Initial imaging demonstrated a retroperitoneal inflammatory mass encasing the infrarenal aorta without evidence of pseudoaneurysm. Repeat imaging two weeks later demonstrated interval development of a pseudoaneurysm, raising concern for an infected aortic process. The patient underwent midline exploratory laparotomy with definitive surgical management and subsequently completed six weeks of intravenous antimicrobial therapy. He had an uncomplicated recovery with resolution of the infection and no reported recurrence. Conclusions Mycotic pseudoaneurysm of the abdominal aorta should be considered in patients with systemic or localized infection and new, unexplained back or abdominal pain, particularly when inflammatory changes surround the aorta on imaging. Serial imaging may be critical for identifying rapid progression from periaortic inflammation to pseudoaneurysm formation. Early recognition and definitive surgical management combined with prolonged antimicrobial therapy can prevent rupture and improve outcomes.

title: Learning Adaptive Gated Fusion of Convolutional and Transformer Features for Generalizable Medical Image Classification
abstract: Abstract Accurate and generalizable classification of medical images remains a central challenge for computer aided diagnosis because convolutional neural networks capture fine grained local texture while vision transformers capture long range global structure, and existing hybrid designs typically combine the two with a fixed rule that cannot adjust to the varying diagnostic importance of local versus global cues across imaging domains [12, 22, 37]. This paper proposes DACANet, a dual path network in which an EfficientNet backbone and a vision transformer backbone extract complementary features that are combined through a learned adaptive gating mechanism, allowing the network to decide, per sample, how much weight to place on local convolutional evidence relative to global transformer evidence before classification. The network was evaluated on three public datasets spanning three diagnostic domains, dermoscopic skin lesion images from HAM10000, magnetic resonance images of brain tumors, and retinal fundus images for diabetic retinopathy grading from APTOS 2019, without any dataset specific tuning. DACANet achieved a best validation accuracy of 87.37 percent on HAM10000, 95.25 percent on the brain tumor dataset, and 84.64 percent on APTOS 2019. An ablation study replacing the adaptive gate with a fixed fusion rule showed adaptive gating improved accuracy on the two more visually heterogeneous datasets by 1.65 and 0.68 percentage points respectively, while performing within 0.19 percentage points of the fixed baseline on the simpler brain tumor dataset. These findings indicate that adaptive fusion is most beneficial when the relative importance of local and global cues varies across samples, offering a practical, reproducible framework for trustworthy, cross domain medical image classification, in line with Sustainable Development Goal 9 on industry, innovation and infrastructure.

An ablation study replacing the adaptive gate with a fixed fusion rule showed adaptive gating improved accuracy on the two more visually heterogeneous datasets by 1.65 and 0.68 percentage points respectively, while performing within 0.19 percentage points of the fixed baseline on the simpler brain tumor dataset. These findings indicate that adaptive fusion is most beneficial when the relative importance of local and global cues varies across samples, offering a practical, reproducible framework for trustworthy, cross domain medical image classification, in line with Sustainable Development Goal 9 on industry, innovation and infrastructure.

title: CT-Based Radiomic Models for Stage Stratification and Relapse Prediction in Colon Cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose: To develop and validate computed tomography (CT)-based radiomic models for differentiating stage II from stage III colon cancer and predicting 5-year relapse risk. Materials and Methods: In this retrospective single-center study, 104 patients with colon cancer who underwent preoperative CT between December 2016 and September 2022 were included. Primary tumors were manually segmented in three dimensions, and 105 radiomic features were extracted together with preoperative clinical variables. The dataset was randomly divided into a training cohort (70%) and an independent validation cohort (30%). Model development and optimization were performed using 10-fold cross-validation within the training cohort. Separate machine learning models were developed for stage differentiation (n = 84) and 5-year relapse prediction (n = 104). Model performance was evaluated in the validation cohort using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results: For stage differentiation, the generalized linear model achieved an AUC of 0.760 in the validation cohort, with a balanced accuracy of 0.744 and a sensitivity of 0.889 for identifying stage II disease. For 5-year relapse prediction, the partial least squares model showed the highest performance, with an AUC of 0.910 and a sensitivity of 0.950. Subgroup analyses demonstrated consistent predictive performance in stage II (AUC, 0.929) and stage III disease (AUC, 0.926). Conclusion: CT-derived radiomic features enabled differentiation between stage II and stage III colon cancer and showed prognostic value for predicting 5-year relapse. These findings support the potential role of radiomics as a noninvasive imaging biomarker for preoperative risk stratification in colon cancer.

title: Low-grade Oncocytic Fumarate Hydratase-deficient Renal Cell Carcinoma in a Patient with Hereditary Leiomyomatosis and Renal Cell Carcinoma Syndrome: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Fumarate hydratase (FH)-deficient renal cell carcinoma (RCC) is generally an aggressive, high-grade tumor with a poor prognosis. We report a case of low-grade oncocytic FH-deficient RCC with a favorable course and discuss it in the context of the genotype-phenotype relationship in FH-deficient RCC. Case presentation: A woman in her 70s was found to have bilateral multifocal renal tumors on PET-CT performed during the work-up of a left cervical mass. She underwent robot-assisted partial nephrectomy of the left kidney. Histopathology showed a low-grade oncocytic renal tumor (pT1aNXMX, WHO/ISUP grade 2) without sarcomatoid change or necrosis, and immunohistochemistry demonstrated loss of FH expression with 2SC positivity, establishing the diagnosis of low-grade oncocytic FH-deficient RCC. Germline genetic testing identified a heterozygous FH missense variant, c.584T > C (p.Met195Thr), confirming hereditary leiomyomatosis and renal cell carcinoma (HLRCC) syndrome. The pedigree showed maternal-line uterine leiomyomatosis consistent with autosomal dominant transmission. The postoperative course was uneventful, with no recurrence or metastasis. The cervical mass proved to be a benign thyroid nodule unrelated to the renal tumor. Conclusion FH-deficient RCC can present as a low-grade, organ-confined tumor with a favorable course. The identical germline FH variant (p.Met195Thr) has elsewhere caused an aggressive tumor, underscoring that the germline genotype does not by itself determine prognosis. Management according to FH-deficient RCC and genetic counseling of relatives remain essential.

title: CSF Diversion Facilitates Further Systemic Therapy in Leptomeningeal Hydrocephalus
abstract: Abstract Background Leptomeningeal disease (LMD) is a complication of metastatic cancer frequently accompanied by symptomatic hydrocephalus. CSF shunting has traditionally been considered palliative, providing symptomatic relief. In the era of CNS-penetrating systemic therapies, factors associated with post-shunt outcomes remain incompletely characterized. We evaluated clinical outcomes following CSF shunting for LMD-associated hydrocephalus and identified predictors of oncologic benefit. Methods We performed a retrospective cohort study of 51 consecutive patients with LMD-associated hydrocephalus who underwent CSF shunting. Clinical, radiographic, molecular, treatment, and outcome data were collected. The primary endpoint was symptomatic improvement and receipt of post-shunt oncologic therapy. Secondary endpoints included overall survival (OS), estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method and Cox regression. Results We included 51 patients with a median pre-shunt KPS of 60. Brain metastases were present in 60.8% and breast cancer (43.1%) was the most common. Clinical improvement occurred in 40 of 49 evaluable patients (81.6%), with the greatest improvement in nausea/vomiting (62.5%) and headache (58.1%). Following shunting, 41 patients (80.4%) received additional oncologic therapy, including 20 (39.2%) who received CNS-penetrating therapy. Median OS was 70 days (95% CI, 54–156). CNS-penetrating therapy was associated with longer survival (193 vs. 49 days; log-rank p = 0.0001). In multivariable analysis, cranial nerve involvement was independently associated with worse survival (HR 4.25, 95% CI 1.75–10.32; p = 0.001), whereas post-shunt therapy (HR 0.078, 95% CI 0.022–0.282; p < 0.001) and CNS-penetrating therapy (HR 0.266, 95% CI 0.116–0.612; p = 0.002) were associated with improved survival. Brain metastases were also associated with inferior survival (HR 2.86, 95% CI 1.10–7.46; p = 0.032). Conclusions CSF shunting provides meaningful symptomatic benefit in patients with LMD-associated hydrocephalus and enables subsequent treatment. Receipt of CNS-penetrating therapy was associated with prolonged survival, whereas cranial nerve involvement and brain metastases identified patients with poorer prognosis. These findings support integrating CSF diversion with contemporary CNS-active therapies in selected patients with LMD.

title: A Tensor Greedy Double-Block Extended Kaczmarz Method for Inconsistent Tensor Linear Systems under the t-product
abstract: Abstract The randomized extended Kaczmarz method is an effective iterative framework for solving large-scale inconsistent linear systems. In this paper, we extend this framework to third-order inconsistent tensor linear systems under the t-product and propose the Tensor Greedy Double Block Extended Kaczmarz (TGDBEK) method. At each iteration, TGDBEK dynamically constructs active blocks of row and column slices via a residual-based greedy selection strategy, prioritizing the slices associated with the largest residual norms. Unlike existing tensor block Kaczmarz variants that rely on static, predefined partitions --- the tensor randomized extended block Kaczmarz (TREBK) method, its greedy counterpart (TREGBK), and the tensor randomized extended average block Kaczmarz (TREABK) method --- TGDBEK adapts the active block sizes dynamically at each step using a single intuitive threshold parameter $\eta$. We establish the theoretical linear convergence of TGDBEK to the unique minimum-norm least-squares solution $\mathcal{A}^\dagger * \mathcal{B}$. Extensive numerical benchmarks on synthetic dense and sparse tensor systems, as well as multidimensional multichannel color and 3D volumetric MRI image deblurring problems, demonstrate that TGDBEK substantially outperforms state-of-the-art tensor Kaczmarz solvers in both iteration count and CPU running time.

title: Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI) in Lung Cancer: A Computer Vision Protocol for Identifying Therapeutic Targets under Simulated Microgravity
abstract: Abstract Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remains among the leading causes of cancer mortality worldwide, due to its high phenotypic plasticity, biomechanical adaptation, and resistance to available treatments. Although precision oncology has advanced significantly through the genomic and molecular characterization of tumors, current approaches still present limitations in capturing the dynamic mechanobiological alterations that influence tumor progression and therapeutic response. Considering that lung tissue is continually subjected to physiological cycles of expansion and retraction during respiration, NSCLC cells develop a cytoskeletal organization that is highly adaptive to the mechanical forces of the microenvironment. ​This study proposes the application of the Mechanobiological Vulnerability Index (MVI), a computational index previously developed for evaluating mechanobiological vulnerability in solid tumors, to quantify structural alterations in three-dimensional NSCLC spheroids subjected to simulated microgravity. The protocol integrates three-dimensional spheroid culture, rotating wall bioreactors (Rotating Cell Culture System – RCCS), and a hybrid computer vision pipeline combining U-Net-based semantic segmentation with Vision Transformer (ViT) architectures. Based on the temporal analysis of cellular deformations, parameters related to plasma membrane deformation, cytoskeletal organization, mechanotransduction, and the exposure of cryptic epitopes are estimated and subsequently integrated into the MVI calculation. ​The central hypothesis of the work is that simulated microgravity induces a progressive perturbation of the biomechanical stability of tumor spheroids, producing a transient window of greater structural vulnerability that can be quantified by the MVI. The identification of this transition could contribute to the future development of mechanobiological biomarkers capable of assisting in the temporal optimization of therapeutic interventions. ​Instead of proposing a definitive therapeutic strategy, this work presents a methodological protocol that integrates mechanobiology, artificial intelligence, and computer vision to investigate the biomechanical adaptation of lung tumors under simulated microgravity conditions. It is expected that this approach will establish a reproducible platform for future experimental studies and contribute to the development of strategies based on the physical properties of the tumor microenvironment in precision oncology.

title: Giant Fibroepithelial Stromal Polyp of the Vulva Mimicking a Malignant Neoplasm: A Rare Case Report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Fibroepithelial polyps (FEPs) of the vulva are uncommon benign mesenchymal lesions that typically measure less than 5 cm. Giant pedunculated FEPs arising from the labia majora are exceptionally rare and can clinically mimic malignant neoplasms. Case Presentation: We report a 29-year-old nulliparous, unmarried woman who presented with a rapidly enlarging, ulcerated, pedunculated vulvar mass arising from the right labia majora. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a pedunculated cutaneous and subcutaneous soft-tissue mass measuring 9.4 × 6.4 × 4.6 cm, with heterogeneous nodular enhancement suggestive of a vascularized tumor. The mass was completely excised at its pedicle base, with intraoperative ligation of two bleeding vessels at the stalk. Histopathology revealed a fibrovascular stromal core covered by stratified squamous epithelium, consistent with a fibroepithelial polyp, with foci of hemorrhagic infarction attributed to torsion of the stalk; no atypia or malignant features were identified. At one-month postoperative follow-up, the surgical site had healed normally. Conclusions: Giant vulvar FEPs are rare benign tumors that can mimic malignancy because of their unusual size, ulceration, and discharge, particularly with rapid growth. Complete surgical excision with secure control of the pedicle is curative, and histopathological confirmation is essential to exclude sarcomas and other soft-tissue neoplasms. This entity should be kept in the differential diagnosis of large vulvar masses to avoid misdiagnosis and unnecessary aggressive intervention. Short-term clinical follow-up is advisable to confirm healing and detect rare complications such as torsion-related infarction.

title: Patient-Specific 3D-Printed Prosthetic Reconstruction of Proximal Tibial Bone Defects: A Retrospective Case Series
abstract: Abstract Background Complex proximal tibial defects after tumor resection require restoration of osseous support, stable fixation, and periarticular soft-tissue function. We evaluated the feasibility, early radiographic stability, complications, and functional outcomes of patient-specific three-dimensional (3D)-printed prosthetic reconstruction. Methods We retrospectively reviewed 13 consecutive patients with proximal tibial bone tumors treated between January and June 2025. All underwent tumor resection and reconstruction with a patient-specific 3D-printed prosthesis and had at least 12 months of follow-up. CT- and MRI-based planning was performed collaboratively by surgeons and engineers. Prostheses incorporated multipoint fixation, porous bone-contact interfaces, and suture holes for soft-tissue reconstruction; expandable components were used in selected pediatric and adolescent patients. Preoperative and 12-month Musculoskeletal Tumor Society 1993 (MSTS-93) scores were compared using the Wilcoxon signed-rank test. Binary outcomes were reported with Clopper-Pearson exact 95% confidence intervals. Results The cohort included 7 male and 6 female patients, with a mean age of 17.8 ± 5.8 years. Diagnoses were Ewing sarcoma in 7 patients, chondrosarcoma in 4, and osteosarcoma in 2. Mean follow-up was 13.1 ± 1.3 months. The median MSTS-93 score increased from 14 (range, 11–15) preoperatively to 26 (range, 22–27) at 12 months, with a median improvement of 12 points (range, 10–15; P < 0.001). No prosthetic fracture, progressive loosening, or interface failure requiring revision occurred. Three adverse events occurred in 2 patients: poor wound healing with superficial infection in one and transient knee dislocation in another. No prosthesis was removed, and no local recurrence or distant metastasis was observed. Conclusions Patient-specific 3D-printed prostheses may provide a reconstructive option for selected complex proximal tibial defects by integrating anatomic matching, fixation, and soft-tissue reconstruction. These short-term findings support preliminary feasibility and early stability but do not establish superiority over conventional reconstruction. Larger comparative studies with longer follow-up are required.

title: Gelfoam-Induced Acute Cauda Equina Syndrome Following L3–L5 Decompression and Instrumented Fusion: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Absorbable gelatin sponge (Gelfoam) is a widely used hemostatic material in spinal surgery. Although generally safe, rare but devastating compressive neurological complications have been reported in intracranial, cervical, and thoracic procedures. Case presentation: A 71‑year‑old Chinese male underwent L3-L5 laminectomy, bilateral L3/4 and L4/5 foraminotomy, pedicle screw fixation, and cage implantation with autogenous bone graft for symptomatic lumbar spinal stenosis. An intact sheet of Gelfoam was placed over the dura for hemostasis and left in situ at wound closure. Upon awakening from anesthesia two hours after surgery, the patient developed severe right lower extremity motor weakness, with muscle strength of 1/5 in the quadriceps, tibialis anterior, extensor hallucis longus, and extensor digitorum longus. On postoperative day 2, emergency lumbar spine CT revealed significant cauda equina compression at L4/5, prompting emergency surgical exploration and decompression. Intraoperatively, an expanded Gelfoam mass with adjacent clot was found circumferentially compressing the dural sac and cauda equina nerve roots from L3 to L5. The entire material was removed, and bilateral nerve root canals were further decompressed. Post‑decompression MRI confirmed complete relief of canal compromise. Muscle strength improved substantially, with all affected groups recovering to 3/5 except the extensor hallucis longus (2/5). Epidural drainage output was only 20 mL and 35 mL on the first two days after the second surgery, supporting that the compression was predominantly Gelfoam mass effect rather than an expanding hematoma. Conclusions : Placement of an intact, unprepared Gelfoam sheet in a closed epidural space can induce hyperacute cauda equina syndrome dominated by motor deficits within hours after surgery, a pattern distinctly different from the previously reported delayed onset of 10-14 days. Indwelling Foley catheterization may mask urinary retention, a classic autonomic warning sign, and delay early recognition. Strict adherence to standardized intraoperative protocols-soaking in thrombin, squeezing to expel air, using only small pieces, and removing residual material after hemostasis-is essential to prevent swelling‑induced mass effect. For patients presenting with severe unilateral lower extremity weakness immediately after surgery and no evidence of hardware misplacement on CT, urgent lumbar MRI and prompt decompression are recommended to maximize neurological recovery.

title: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Ophthalmic Foundation Models with Point-Based Classification and Retrieval
abstract: Abstract General-purpose vision foundation models have been evaluated across a wide range of tasks to demonstrate the versatility of their learned representations. By contrast, ophthalmic foundation models have largely been assessed using a narrow set of downstream tasks, primarily disease classification and segmentation, providing only a limited view of their representational capabilities. Considering how clinicians interpret ophthalmic images, where disease-relevant clinical signs are identified before diagnosis, we introduced an ophthalmic foundation model evaluation framework comprising two tasks: 1) point-supervised disease classification and 2) point-guided clinical sign-based image retrieval. Each task incorporates sparse point annotations indicating disease-relevant evidence locations. We applied this approach to diabetic retinopathy using colour fundus photography (CFP) and age-related macular degeneration using both CFP and optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans. Our evaluation spanned 11 foundation models across four newly curated and six established datasets. The results reveal that existing ophthalmic foundation models, despite their strong performance on disease classification, still struggle with the clinical sign retrieval task, although they outperform general-purpose foundation models. Our findings highlight the need to improve these models' capabilities at the fine-grained sign-level. We publicly release our benchmark to facilitate further research on ophthalmic foundation models.

We applied this approach to diabetic retinopathy using colour fundus photography (CFP) and age-related macular degeneration using both CFP and optical coherence tomography (OCT) scans. Our evaluation spanned 11 foundation models across four newly curated and six established datasets. The results reveal that existing ophthalmic foundation models, despite their strong performance on disease classification, still struggle with the clinical sign retrieval task, although they outperform general-purpose foundation models. Our findings highlight the need to improve these models' capabilities at the fine-grained sign-level. We publicly release our benchmark to facilitate further research on ophthalmic foundation models.

title: Adenocarcinoma of the Minor Duodenal Papilla Mimicking a Pancreatic Head Tumor: A Rare Case Report and Review of the Literature
abstract: Abstract Background Adenocarcinoma of the minor duodenal papilla (papilla of Santorini) is an exceptionally rare periampullary malignancy, with only a small number of cases reported in the literature. Its close anatomical relationship with the pancreatic head and duodenum can make determination of the primary site difficult, particularly after local invasion. Case presentation: A 72-year-old woman presented with progressive dysphagia, early satiety, epigastric pain, vomiting, and significant weight loss. Endoscopy demonstrated stenosis of the second portion of the duodenum, while computed tomography and endoscopic ultrasonography revealed an approximately 3-cm lesion in the pancreatic-head/uncinate region. Neither the common bile duct nor the main pancreatic duct was dilated, and the patient had no clinical or biochemical evidence of obstructive jaundice. Serum carbohydrate antigen 19 − 9 was markedly elevated at 7,619 U/mL. Following preoperative optimization, pancreaticoduodenectomy was performed. Histopathological examination demonstrated adenocarcinoma centered on the minor duodenal papilla, extending through the duodenal wall and superficially invading the pancreas, while the major papilla and common bile duct remained uninvolved. Surgical margins were negative, perineural invasion was present, and all 12 examined lymph nodes were negative for metastatic disease. The pathological stage was reported as pT3N0M0. Conclusion Minor duodenal papilla adenocarcinoma may mimic a pancreatic-head malignancy and can progress without biliary obstruction because of its anatomical separation from the common bile duct. Local invasion may further obscure its site of origin, potentially contributing to underrecognition among tumors classified as pancreatic or periampullary adenocarcinomas. Careful correlation of radiological, endoscopic, operative, and histopathological findings is therefore essential for accurate diagnosis.

title: A Reference-Based Approach Using Whole-Brain Segmentation for Image-Derived Blood Activity Concentration in CBV Quantification
abstract: Abstract Quantitative imaging of cerebral blood flow (CBF), oxygen extraction fraction (OEF), cerebral metabolic rate of oxygen (CMRO 2 ), and cerebral blood volume (CBV) using 15 O-labeled compounds is useful for evaluating cerebral ischemia. However, quantitative PET requires measurement of blood activity concentration, which is typically obtained by arterial blood sampling. Although image-derived input function methods have been developed for CBF, OEF, and CMRO 2 quantification, a non-invasive method for obtaining blood activity concentration for CBV measurement has not been established. This study aimed to develop and validate a reference-based method for estimating blood activity concentration from C 15 O PET images. Among 186 subjects, mean CBV and the coefficient of variation (CV) were calculated for each brain segment in 64 subjects (Group A; moyamoya disease (MMD) present/absent, 20/44 ) . In an independent cohort of 122 subjects (Group B; MMD present/absent, 35/87), blood activity concentration was estimated for each brain segment by reproducing the reference mean CBV obtained from Group A. The segment-based estimates were combined using CV-weighted averaging. The estimated blood activity concentrations were compared with those obtained by arterial blood sampling. The mean ± SD of CBV across all segments in Group A was 0.039 ± 0.011 ml/g overall, 0.037 ± 0.009 ml/g in subjects without MMD, and 0.043 ± 0.012 ml/g in subjects with MMD. In Group B, the percentage differences between image-derived and measured blood activity concentrations were 0.35 ± 9.8%, − 1.4 ± 8.8%, and 4.8 ± 10.6% in the overall, MMD-absent, and MMD-present groups, respectively, using the all-segment approach. When the CBV-matched segment approach was applied, the corresponding differences were − 0.60 ± 8.8%, − 1.4 ± 8.4%, and 1.5 ± 9.4%, respectively. The image-derived blood activity concentrations showed good agreement with those obtained by arterial blood sampling, and the CBV-matched segment approach reduced the difference in the MMD-present group. The proposed method may enable non-invasive and automated estimation of blood activity concentration for quantitative CBV measurement without arterial blood sampling.

title: Prognostic impact of PSMA PET-CT and conventional imaging staging for cN0M0 intermediate/high-risk localized prostate cancer undergoing extraperitoneal laparoscopic radical prostatectomy with or without standard pelvic lymph node dissection
abstract: Abstract Background Prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PSMA PET-CT) has been validated as a high-performance imaging modality with markedly improved diagnostic accuracy for patients with prostate cancer (PCa). Nevertheless, its differential prognostic value compared with conventional imaging (CI) remains poorly characterized among patients with cN0M0 localized PCa undergoing extraperitoneal laparoscopic radical prostatectomy (eLRP), particularly regarding the clinical decision to perform concurrent standard pelvic lymph node dissection (sPLND). Objective To compare oncological outcomes after eLRP±sPLND between cN0M0 PCa patients staged by PSMA PET-CT and CI. Methods and Materials We retrospectively enrolled biopsy-proven cN0M0 PCa patients who underwent eLRP. Patients were split into PSMA PET-CT and CI cohorts, each further stratified into PLND and non-PLND subgroups. Baseline imbalance was adjusted via inverse probability weighting (IPW). Kaplan–Meier survival analysis was used to estimate biochemical recurrence-free survival (bRFS) and metastasis-free survival (MFS). Univariate and multivariate Cox proportional hazards regression models were constructed to identify independent clinicopathological prognostic factors. A two-sided P value < 0.05 was defined as statistically significant. Results 369 patients (162 in PSMA PET-CT cohort and 207 in CI cohort) were included, with intermediate/high-risk disease predominating in both cohorts (95.1% vs 97.6%). Pathological nodal metastasis was significantly less frequent in the PSMA PET-CT (4.8% vs.11.0%, p < 0.001). No significant bRFS differences existed between PSMA PET-CT and CI cohort regardless of sPLND performance (all p > 0.05), though non-PLND patients with PSMA PET-CT staging showed a favorable bRFS trend. MFS was comparable between the two imaging modalities in the PLND subgroup (p = 0.137), while PSMA PET-CT staging was associated with a significantly better MFS compared with CI in the non-PLND subgroup (HR = 0.205, 95% CI 0.047–0.903; p = 0.036). Conclusions PSMA PET-CT outperforms CI for preoperative nodal staging in intermediate/high-risk localized PCa. sPLND may be omitted for cN0M0 patients staged by PSMA PET-CT, while routine sPLND is mandatory for those staged by CI before eLRP.

title: Long-term radiographic marginal bone changes and implant survival in tooth agenesis versus non-agenesis sites: a retrospective cohort study of 710 implants
abstract: Abstract Purpose Tooth agenesis is associated with reduced alveolar ridge dimensions and altered local anatomy, potentially affecting implant long-term outcomes. This study compared marginal bone loss (MBL), implant survival, and implant success between implants placed in agenesis and non-agenesis sites. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 316 patients with 710 implants placed between 2000 and 2010. Implants in tooth agenesis sites (TA group, n = 284) were compared with implants in normally developed alveolar bone (control group, n = 426). Mesial and distal MBL were assessed radiographically at short-term (1–<3 years), mid-term (3–<8 years), and long-term (≥ 8 years) follow-up. Survival was evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis, and success was assessed according to the Albrektsson, Buser, and Misch criteria. Results Bone augmentation was required less frequently in the TA group than in controls (34.5% vs. 43.0%; p = 0.028). MBL increased over time in both groups, without significant between-group differences at any follow-up interval. Implant survival was comparable between groups (TA: 96.1%; control: 93.9%; p = 0.604). Success rates were similar according to the Buser and Misch criteria, whereas the Albrektsson criteria indicated lower radiographic success in the TA group. Combined internal and external augmentation was associated with significantly lower survival than either procedure alone (p = 0.003). Conclusions Implants placed in tooth agenesis sites showed long-term bone stability and survival comparable to controls. These findings suggest that local anatomical conditions and reconstructive complexity may influence long-term implant prognosis more strongly than tooth agenesis itself.

title: Ultra-Early Postmortem 3-T MRI of the Human Brain: A Two-Case Feasibility Study of Structural, Diffusion, and Vascular Imaging in Unfixed Cadavers
abstract: Abstract Background Cadaveric magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) permits high-resolution, motion-free characterization of neuroanatomy, but postmortem interval, tissue temperature, autolysis, and chemical fixation can alter relaxation and diffusion properties. Imaging rapidly after death and before fixation may reduce exposure to these time-dependent changes, but the feasibility of combining sub-millimeter structural imaging, advanced diffusion imaging, and vascular imaging on a clinical 3T platform remains incompletely characterized. We therefore assessed the technical feasibility of these acquisitions in a two-cadaver exploratory series. Methods This exploratory two-case feasibility series included two adult cadavers studied at a short postmortem interval on a clinical 3T MRI system. Acquisitions included T1-weighted MPRAGE, T2-weighted SPACE, susceptibility-weighted imaging, diffusion spectrum imaging, multi-shell diffusion-weighted imaging, and time-of-flight angiography. In one specimen, postmortem vascular perfusion with manganese chloride was followed by additional angiographic imaging. Structural, diffusion, and vascular datasets underwent modality-specific preprocessing, reconstruction, and visual quality review. Feasibility was evaluated descriptively; no inferential statistical tests or population-level effect estimates were performed. Results Sub-millimeter structural MRI and advanced diffusion imaging were acquired and reconstructed in both specimens. Whole-brain deterministic tractography was generated in both cases. In specimen 1, a focal structural abnormality compatible with a chronic lacunar infarct was accompanied by a visually reduced streamline representation in the corresponding region. In the perfused specimen, post-perfusion angiographic imaging enabled visualization and 3D reconstruction of major proximal intracranial vessels and showed reduced distal vascular opacification in the right middle cerebral artery territory. These focal structural, diffusion, and vascular observations were exploratory rather than prespecified diagnostic endpoints. Conclusions In this two-specimen series, ultra-early unfixed cadaveric MRI on a standard clinical 3T platform yielded interpretable high-resolution structural and diffusion datasets, with a technically usable vascular reconstruction in the perfused case. These findings support workflow feasibility but do not establish diagnostic accuracy, preservation of in vivo tissue properties, reproducibility, or generalizability.

title: Sphere-based representation of image-resolved porous media
abstract: Abstract The Multi-Sphere Shape (MSS) algorithm is applied to generate sphere-based representations of porous media directly from segmented volumetric image data. The solid or void phase is approximated by overlapping spheres, providing a simplified representation for particle-based simulations. The sphere centers lie on the medial axis of the selected phase without requiring explicit medial-axis extraction. The approach is demonstrated for the pore space of a ceramic foam reconstructed from computed tomography (CT) data, where 22,468 spheres represent 95\% of a volume comprising 64 million voxels. For sphere-dominated morphologies, the sphere sizes, overlaps, and connectivity additionally provide structural descriptors such as pore sizes, throat areas, and coordination numbers. The resulting representation therefore combines a simplified simulation model with direct access to structural information.

title: Medical Artificial Intelligence: A Multimodal, Human-Centered, Domain-Adaptive Framework for Surgical Decision Support and Patient Safety
abstract: Abstract Background Surgical decision-making is complex, time-sensitive, and dependent on heterogeneous clinical information. Artificial intelligence (AI) has been investigated for risk prediction, medical imaging, intraoperative video analysis, and clinical decision support, but translation from model development to safe clinical use remains limited by generalizability, uncertainty, human-factors, and governance challenges. Methods We developed an evidence-informed conceptual framework for multimodal surgical decision support. A targeted literature synthesis was performed using peer-reviewed and regulatory sources published from 2020 through 28 August 2026, with emphasis on surgical AI, clinical prediction, multimodal systems, human-AI interaction, explainability, patient safety, validation, and AI governance. The framework specifies intended use, input modalities, modular AI architecture, domain adaptation, uncertainty estimation, safety controls, clinician interaction, validation stages, post-deployment monitoring, and regulatory lifecycle requirements. No patient-level dataset was analyzed, no model was trained, and no new clinical performance estimates were generated. Results The framework defines a traceable pipeline from multimodal clinical data to clinician-reviewed decision support and explicitly separates proposed architecture from evidence reported in the literature. Literature-derived evidence demonstrates substantial potential for surgical AI but also identifies important validation gaps. In a 36-study scoping review of AI-enabled surgical decision support, 80.6% of studies used internal validation only, 13.8% used external validation, and 5.6% used real-time validation; none evaluated clinical implementation efficacy. A 2024 systematic review of 102 clinically validated surgical AI studies similarly reported heterogeneous validation quality. These findings support staged validation rather than universal performance claims. No prospective clinical efficacy claim is made in the present framework. Conclusion A domain-adaptive, multimodal architecture can organize future surgical AI development around safety, transparency, human oversight, and reproducibility. Clinical effectiveness remains to be established through task-specific development, temporal and external validation, silent prospective deployment, human-AI evaluation, and prospective clinical studies.

title: A Comparative Study of Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN, and YOLOv8 for Object Detection and Instance Segmentation, with a Custom-Class Transfer-Learning Case Study
abstract: Abstract Object detection and instance segmentation are foundational tasks in computer vision, underpinning applications ranging from autonomous driving to medical imaging and defense surveillance. This paper presents a structured, reproducible comparison of three influential detection architectures — Faster R-CNN, Mask R-CNN, and YOLOv8 — spanning the two-stage, mask-augmented, and single-stage detection paradigms. I first re-derive and consolidate the theoretical foundations that connect these architectures, tracing the lineage from R-CNN and Fast R-CNN through the Region Proposal Network (RPN) innovation that defines Faster R-CNN, and onward to the RoIAlign-based mask branch of Mask R-CNN and the anchor-free, single-pass design of YOLOv8. I then evaluate the three models qualitatively, both on general-purpose COCO-domain imagery and on a purpose-built, hand-annotated dataset for a domain the pretrained COCO label space does not cover: military armored vehicles ("tanks"). Using CVAT.ai-annotated bounding boxes and a YOLOv8s model fine-tuned via transfer learning, I show that a lightweight, single-stage detector can be adapted to a novel class with a small annotated corpus and modest compute, while two-stage detectors trained only on COCO systematically mislabel the same objects as "truck" or "car." I further situate the study within the rapidly evolving 2024–2026 detection landscape, discussing how transformer-based real-time detectors (RT-DETR, RF-DETR) and newer YOLO variants (YOLOv9-YOLOv12) extend the accuracy-speed frontier established by the models benchmarked here. I conclude with a discussion of the practical trade-offs between detection accuracy, inference latency, computational cost, and annotation burden, and I outline the quantitative benchmarking protocol — mAP, precision-recall, and frames-per-second measurement across matched training conditions — needed to extend this qualitative and architectural comparison into a fully numeric one.

title: Semi-Automated Quantitative CT–Enhanced GAP Index for Prognostic Assessment in Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis
abstract: Abstract Background Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) is marked by spatially heterogeneous fibrotic remodeling and highly variable clinical trajectories, which limit the precision of existing prognostic tools. Widely used indices, such as GAP (Gender–Age–Physiology), rely on physiological measurements and do not explicitly capture anatomical disease burden. Advances in artificial intelligence (AI)–assisted 3D quantitative Computed Tomography (CT) imaging enable objective, volumetric characterization of lung fibrosis and provide a foundation for radiology-integrated prognostic modeling. Methods We developed and evaluated an AI-assisted quantitative CT framework for prognostic assessment in patients with IPF. Whole-lung segmentation was performed using a pretrained deep learning model (LungMask), followed by semi-automated segmentation of fibrotic abnormalities with radiologist-guided refinement. Quantitative imaging biomarkers, including honeycombing volume, non-honeycomb fibrotic lung volume, preserved lung volume, and the pathological lung volume-to-total lung volume ratio, were derived from 3D CT analysis. This radiological parameter was integrated into the conventional GAP index to create a radiology-enhanced prognostic model. Prognostic performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis, and Kaplan–Meier survival analysis. title: A Gigantic Heterogenous Silent Corticotroph Pituitary Neuroendocrine Tumour With Posterior Fossa Cyst and a Fibrotic Wall—Diagnostic Mimicry and Route-Tailored Staging: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Neurosurgical route selection for treating silent corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumours is complicated because of their nature of mimicking aggressive skull-base disease. Case presentation: A 21-year-old man with a background of autism spectrum disorder presented with headache, diplopia, right third cranial nerve palsy and visual blurring. A giant heterogeneous sellar–suprasellar mass with cavernous sinus/internal carotid artery involvement and a posterior fossa cyst compressing the brainstem is shown on MRI. He has a normal baseline pituitary test result. Endoscopic endonasal transsphenoidal debulking achieved diagnosis and decompression; histology confirmed a silent corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumour (adrenocorticotropic hormone-positive, limited T-box pituitary transcription factor. Post-operative diabetes insipidus occurred. On surveillance, the cyst enlarged with hydrocephalus. Two Ommaya attempts failed due to a taut, fibrotic wall. Right craniotomy enabled lateral debulking and direct cyst cannulation with effective decompression. Residual cavernous/internal carotid artery-adjacent disease was treated with proton beam therapy (50.4 Gy/28 fractions) without notable acute toxicity. Bulbar function and third-nerve palsy improved post-craniotomy; gait and speech improved after radiotherapy. Imaging showed reduced brainstem compression with a manageable residual; visual acuity remained 6/21 right, 6/6 left. Conclusions: This case supports route-tailored staging-endonasal decompression, early conversion to transcranial access for fibrotic, catheter-resistant cysts, and consolidative proton therapy-and highlights the value of autism spectrum disorder-adapted pathways and multidisciplinary team oversight.

title: Cross-center sex estimation from patellar CT: multi-feature transformer fusion of morphometry, radiomics, and deep features
abstract: Abstract Patellar computed tomography (CT) images contain sex-dimorphic information; however, single-feature approaches may not fully exploit complementary information. We developed a multi-feature Transformer fusion framework integrating morphometry, radiomics, and deep learning features for sex estimation. We retrospectively included 836 knee CT scans from two centers: an internal dataset ( n = 697, slice thickness 1.5 mm) for model development and internal testing, and an external dataset ( n = 139, slice thickness 1.5–2.0 mm) for external validation. After manual patellar segmentation, we extracted six morphometric parameters, 13 radiomic features selected by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and deep features from two-dimensional (2D) and three-dimensional (3D) ResNet-50 models; these were fused using a Transformer encoder with multi-head self-attention. The framework was evaluated with five-fold cross-validation against single-feature baselines and alternative fusion strategies. On the internal test set, the Transformer fusion model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.972 (95% confidence interval [CI] 0.944–0.992) and accuracy of 0.943, outperforming single-feature models (AUC 0.918–0.935) and fusion baselines. On the external dataset, AUC was 0.942 and accuracy 0.879. Performance was comparable to forensic experts with a > 90% reduction in processing time. Self-attention adaptively weighted complementary features, maintaining accuracy across acquisition protocols and reducing inter- and intra-observer variability. Thinner slices benefited radiomic and deep learning models, whereas morphometric features remained stable. These findings suggest the framework provides accurate, generalizable sex estimation from patellar CT, supporting its potential as an objective forensic tool extendable to other skeletal sites.

title: Identification of Pulmonary Embolism in Patients With Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease Using Clinical and Non-contrast CT Radiomic Features
abstract: Abstract Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a potentially life-threatening complication in patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), but early recognition is challenging because of substantial overlap in clinical manifestations. We aimed to develop and internally validate a multimodal model integrating clinical variables and radiomic features derived from non-contrast chest computed tomography (CT) to identify concomitant PE in patients with COPD. In this retrospective study, 415 patients with COPD were included, of whom 116 had concomitant PE confirmed by computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA). Radiomic features were extracted from non-contrast chest CT images. Feature selection was performed using a multistep procedure incorporating univariable screening, correlation-based redundancy reduction, minimum redundancy maximum relevance, and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression. Clinical, radiomics, and combined models were developed and internally validated. Model performance was assessed using receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, calibration analysis, and decision curve analysis. The combined model showed the highest discriminative performance, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.987 in the internal test cohort, compared with 0.959 for the clinical model and 0.937 for the radiomics model. The combined model also demonstrated good calibration and yielded greater net clinical benefit across a broad range of threshold probabilities. A multimodal model integrating routinely available clinical variables with radiomic features from non-contrast chest CT showed excellent performance for identifying concomitant PE in patients with COPD. This approach may enable opportunistic PE risk stratification during routine chest CT examinations and help identify patients who may benefit from further CTPA evaluation. External validation is warranted before clinical implementation.

title: A Novel TREX1 Frameshift Variant (c.802del p. (Arg268Glyfs*9) Associated with Retinal Vasculopathy with Cerebral Leukoencephalopathy and Systemic Manifestations: a Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background: Report a Novel TREX1 Frameshift Variant (c.802del p. (Arg268Glyfs*9) associated with Retinal Vasculopathy with Cerebral Leukoencephalopathy and Systemic Manifestations (RVCL-S) and accompanying clinical features of the disease. Case presentation: A 42-year-old male with multiple substance abuse disorder presented to the emergency room in a state of confusion with worsening headaches. Neuroimaging (Computed Tomography scan/ Magnetic Resonance Imaging scan) was performed and brain mass with midline shift was noted. The differential diagnoses included brain abscess versus multiple sclerosis or mass lesion. Extensive workup did not confirm infection or demyelinating disease. Treatment with broad spectrum antibiotics yielded no benefit and brain biopsy showed inflammatory necrosis only. In addition to his brain lesions, peripheral neovascular retinopathy was found and treated with laser photocoagulation. He had a positive family history of retinal vasculopathy with cerebral leukodystrophy (RVCL) affecting father, paternal grandmother, and paternal cousins. Genetic testing showed a pathogenic TREX1 c.802del p. (Arg268Glyfs*9) variant. To our knowledge, this variant and its accompanying clinical features have not been previously reported. Conclusions: Retinal vasculopathy with cerebral leukodystrophy and systemic manifestations (RVCL-S) is a rare, autosomal dominant microangiopathy caused by truncating TREX 1 mutations, characterized by vascular retinopathy, neurological features, cognitive decline, Raynaud’s phenomenon, anemia, and renal and hepatic involvement. The patient developed avascular necrosis of the femur. We describe clinical, ophthalmic, radiographic, and systemic features of this 42-year-old male with the novel TREX1 c.802del p. (Arg268Glyfs*9) variant with a review of the literature. Cerebral lesions with surrounding edema often require corticosteroid therapy and early recognition of RVCL-S may prevent unnecessary invasive procedures. There is no cure and patients are at risk for premature death. A genetic evaluation is essential to establish the diagnosis.

title: The Carcinoembryonic Antigen-to-Skeletal Muscle Index Ratio as a Novel Prognostic Marker in Colorectal Cancer
abstract: Abstract Background Carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) and sarcopenia, defined as a low skeletal muscle index (SMI), are established prognostic factors in colorectal cancer (CRC). We evaluated the prognostic value of the preoperative CEA-to-SMI ratio (CSR), an index integrating tumor burden and host physiological reserve. Methods We retrospectively analyzed 1,033 patients who underwent curative surgery for CRC. SMI (cm²/m²) was measured on preoperative computed tomography at the third lumbar vertebra, and patients were stratified into CSR quartiles (Q1–Q4). The primary endpoint was overall survival (OS). Independent prognostic factors were identified by multivariable Cox regression, and discrimination was compared with that of CEA and SMI alone using Harrell's concordance index (C-index). Results Five-year OS decreased stepwise as the CSR increased: 93.4% (Q1), 86.8% (Q2), 83.2% (Q3) and 76.6% (Q4) ( P < 0.001). On multivariable analysis the CSR remained an independent prognostic factor, with Q4 carrying a higher risk of death than Q1 (hazard ratio 2.650, 95% confidence interval 1.610–4.360; P < 0.001). The C-index of the CSR (0.625) was higher than that of CEA alone (0.574, P < 0.001) or SMI alone (0.574, P = 0.039). Adding the CSR to a base clinical model improved the C-index from 0.714 to 0.728 ( P = 0.041). Conclusion The preoperative CSR is a potentially useful independent prognostic indicator in CRC, providing additive risk stratification beyond CEA or SMI alone and enabling identification of high-risk patients in clinical practice.

title: Selective data curation enables efficient pretraining of chest radiograph foundation models
abstract: Abstract Foundation models for medical imaging are pretrained on increasingly large datasets following a “scale-at-all-costs” paradigm, although medical corpora often contain substantial redundancy, class imbalance and heterogeneous data quality. Here we investigate whether selective data curation can reduce the data and computational requirements of chest X-ray (CXR) vision-language pretraining. We introduce CheXficient, which leverages representation-guided data curation to prioritize informative and important image-report pairs. CheXficient is pretrained using 22.7% of 1,235,004 paired CXR images and reports and under 27.3% of the total compute budget, yet maintains strong performance relative to full-data pretraining and remains competitive with other large-scale pretrained models. We assess CheXficient across 20 individual benchmarks spanning 5 task types, including non-adapted off-the-shelf evaluations (zero-shot findings classification and cross-modal retrieval) and adapted downstream tasks (disease diagnosis, semantic segmentation, and radiology report generation). Further analyses show CheXficient systematically prioritizes under-represented training samples, improving generalizability on long-tailed or rare thoracic conditions. These findings support selective data curation as a practical strategy for resource-efficient development of medical foundation models.

title: Magnetic Resonance Imaging Contrast
abstract: Abstract Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) provides excellent soft‑tissue contrast for anatomical imaging and is a cornerstone of differential diagnosis. However, existing contrast modalities—such as relaxation‑time‑weighted and proton‑density (PD)‑weighted imaging—remain inherently qualitative, limiting the full clinical potential of MRI. To overcome the quantification challenge posed by patient‑specific PD contributions to the MR signal, we propose a contrast‑quantification method (cMRI) based on coherent precession of the magnetization vector. Using conventional fast spin‑echo sequences, our method computes and reconstructs T1‑weighted contrast maps, T2‑weighted contrast maps, as well as T1, T2 and relative PD maps. Preclinical experiments were performed on a child with autism spectrum disorder and on standard phantoms. Under mixed echo‑time conditions, we obtained T1‑ and T2‑weighted contrast maps with values in the range (0, 1), as well as approximate T1 and T2 maps (affected by effective TE) with relaxation times within physiologically plausible ranges for human tissues, and relative PD distributions referenced to a homogeneous phantom. These preliminary results validate the feasibility of the proposed contrast‑quantification approach and open a new avenue for precise and even early imaging‑based differential diagnosis.

title: Comparative Study of Anatomical and Learned Features in AI Models for Structural Brain MRI
abstract: Abstract In this work, we comprehensively evaluate three popular feature-extractionparadigms in AI-based neuroimaging modeling: (1) computation of anatomicalsurfaces and volumes, (2) supervised learning with convolutional neural net-works (CNNs), and (3) unsupervised pretraining of vision transformer (ViT)foundation models, followed by supervised finetuning. Our study is based on18 publicly available datasets containing 3D structural T1-weighted MRI scansfrom approximately 80,000 participants across seven distinct clinical tasks. Weobserve that a linear model based on anatomical features matches the diag-nostic performance of complex nonlinear features learned by sophisticated AIframeworks, including foundation models trained on thousands of scans. Con-versely, CNNs and pretrained ViTs learn features that implicitly capture relevantanatomical information, bypassing the need for explicit feature extraction. Build-ing upon these insights, we propose Anatomy Segmentation Pretraining (ASP),a novel method to incorporate anatomical information during foundation-modelpretraining, which outperforms existing models in biological age estimation.

title: Synthesis, Radiolabeling, and Biological Evaluation of an RGD-Conjugated 99ᵐTc Dendrimer for Breast Cancer SPECT Imaging
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Breast cancer remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Early and accurate molecular imaging is essential for improving diagnosis and patient outcomes. Nanotechnology-based imaging probes offer promising opportunities to overcome limitations associated with tumour heterogeneity. Materials and Methods Third-generation polyethylene glycol (PEG)–citrate dendrimers were synthesised and functionalised with arginylglycylaspartic acid (RGD) peptides targeting αvβ3 integrins. The nanoconjugates were radiolabeled with technetium-99m ( 99 mTc) and characterised using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR), liquid chromatography–mass spectrometry (LC–MS), Fourier-transform infrared (FTIR) spectroscopy, dynamic light scattering (DLS), and electron microscopy. In vitro cytotoxicity was assessed using the XTT assay. In vivo imaging and biodistribution studies were conducted in tumour-bearing nude mice using single-photon emission computed tomography/computed tomography (SPECT/CT). Results The synthesised dendrimers demonstrated favourable physicochemical properties and high radiochemical purity. In vitro assays confirmed good biocompatibility, with no significant cytotoxicity observed at concentrations up to 8 mg/mL. SPECT imaging revealed rapid and specific tumour accumulation within the first hour post-injection, with maximal uptake observed at approximately 90 minutes. Biodistribution studies indicated predominant renal clearance and minimal nonspecific uptake in non-target organs. The radiolabeled nanoconjugates remained stable in human serum for up to 24 hours. Conclusion RGD-functionalized, 99 mTc-labeled PEG–citrate dendrimers exhibit strong potential as targeted SPECT imaging agents for breast cancer. Their favourable targeting specificity, imaging contrast, and pharmacokinetic profile support further development for molecular imaging and theranostic applications.

Their favourable targeting specificity, imaging contrast, and pharmacokinetic profile support further development for molecular imaging and theranostic applications.

title: Time-varying prognostic associations of organ-specific baseline [18F]FDG PET/CT findings in clinically selected colorectal adenocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate organ-specific baseline [18F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) findings and continuous global maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) as correlates of overall survival in clinically selected colorectal adenocarcinoma, including possible variation over follow-up. Methods Among 453 explicitly baseline/staging examinations, 51 with an indication also referring to another primary tumour were excluded, leaving 402 patients. Overall-survival data were valid in 216 patients (90 deaths); the organ-site model included 209 patients (88 deaths) and the SUVmax model 129 patients (60 deaths). Cox models adjusted for age and recorded clinical stage. Proportional-hazards diagnostics prompted exploratory 0-12-month and later analyses. Inverse-probability weighting, bootstrap resampling and a 90-day treatment landmark assessed robustness. Results Liver involvement (hazard ratio [HR] 2.02, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.23–3.32) and nodal disease (HR 2.04, 95% CI 1.15–3.60) were associated with mortality in the simultaneous organ-site model. Exploratory time-split analyses showed stronger early associations for liver and nodal disease and a later association for bone involvement after false-discovery-rate correction. Each doubling of global SUVmax remained associated with mortality after adjustment for age, stage, liver and nodal involvement (HR 1.53, 95% CI 1.15–2.02; p = 0.003). Weighted and landmark analyses were directionally consistent. Conclusion Organ distribution and continuous SUVmax on baseline [18F]FDG PET/CT were associated with overall survival in this selected cohort. Time-varying findings remain exploratory, and missing outcomes, incomplete anatomical/molecular annotation and absent volumetric PET measures preclude clinical risk-model use.

title: Feature Fusion Based Deep Learning Framework for Brain Tumor Classification
abstract: Abstract Classification is considered very important step in diagnosis of serious diseases like brain tumor as it plays an important role in prognosis and successful recovery of the patient. This paper proposes an explainable hybrid deep learning architecture for seven class brain tumor classification using feature-level fusion of six independently fine-tuned pre-trained CNN models: Xception, InceptionV3, VGG16, MobileNetV2, ResNet50, and DenseNet121. Fifteen feature level fusion combinations have been evaluated using a dataset of 11,288 MRI scans representing six tumor classes and one nontumor class: glioma, meningioma, pituitary tumor, astrocytoma, ependymoma, schwannoma. InceptionV3 + VGG16, the hybrid architecture gave best performance according to experimental results attaining test accuracy of 97.87% with outstanding macro and weighted F1-scores of 97.77% and 97.87% subsequently. Further, Grad-CAM and Occlusion Sensitivity Analysis were collectively implemented on classification results of best hybrid model to ensure the clinical relevance of the learned features and offering visual explanations of the classification. Finally, best hybrid model was successfully validated on external dataset of five tumor classes comprising 234 MRI scans to prove its generalization on unseen dataset.

title: Cardiovascular Magnetic Resonance Pulmonary Artery Peak Flow Velocity as a Marker of Pulmonary Vascular Resistance in Fibrotic Interstitial Lung Disease
abstract: Abstract Background. Pulmonary hypertension (PH) is a common and severe complication of interstitial lung disease (ILD), yet early diagnosis remains challenging. Cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) offers non-invasive assessment of pulmonary vascular hemodynamics, but evidence in PH associated with ILD is limited. This study aimed to evaluate the relationship between CMR-derived parameters and invasive hemodynamics in patients with fibrotic ILD. Methods. In this prospective observational study, 41 patients with fibrotic ILD underwent pulmonary function testing, cardiopulmonary exercise testing, transthoracic echocardiography, and CMR. Twenty patients additionally underwent RHC. CMR-derived measurements included ventricular function parameters, heart chamber and great vessel dimensions, and pulmonary artery flow hemodynamic metrics. Associations between CMR parameters, invasive hemodynamics, exercise capacity and symptom burden were assessed using correlation, regression, and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analyses. Results. Among 20 patients who underwent RHC, PH was confirmed in all cases, including 15 with isolated precapillary PH and 5 with combined PH. Pulmonary vascular resistance (PVR) of over 5 Wood units defined severe PH in 6 patients who met the criteria. Pulmonary artery peak flow velocity (PA-Vmax) measured on CMR was significantly higher in the non-severe PH group (81.15 ± 19.27 cm/s vs. 52.33 ± 5.13 cm/s, p < 0.001) and demonstrated promising discriminatory performance for identifying severe PH (AUC 0.923, 95% CI 0.778-1.000, p = 0.004), with a threshold of < 62.5 cm/s yielding 100% sensitivity and 92.3% specificity. An inverse-transformed PA-Vmax model demonstrated a strong association with invasive PVR (R 2 = 0.651, F = 31.65, p < 0.001). Higher PA-Vmax correlated with greater exercise capacity, including higher anaerobic threshold (r = 0.419, p = 0.015) and maximal workload (r = 0.329, p = 0.050). Lower CMR-derived TAPSE was independently associated with greater dyspnea severity (β=-0.426, p = 0.025), while CMR-TAPSE/RHC-mPAP ratio demonstrated an even stronger association with symptom burden (r s =-0.570, p = 0.021). Conclusions. In patients with fibrotic ILD, CMR-derived PA-Vmax was significantly associated with PVR measured by RHC and demonstrated promising discrimination for severe PH in this exploratory cohort. CMR measurements of right ventricular adaptation were associated with functional capacity and dyspnea severity. These findings support further evaluation of CMR as a promising non-invasive modality for pulmonary vascular assessment in fibrotic ILD patients undergoing evaluation for suspected PH.

title: Ultrasound-Guided Precise Acupotomy for Chronic Plantar Fasciitis: A Single-Center Randomized Controlled Trial Focused on Long-Term Effect and Recurrence Rate
abstract: Abstract Background Plantar fasciitis (PF) is a prevalent musculoskeletal condition characterized by localized pain at the calcaneal attachment of the plantar fascia. Its etiology is multifactorial and Treatment methods are diverse.Ultrasound-guided acupotomy is prevalent in recent years for plantar fasciitis .The study aimed To observe the improvement in pain and foot function following ultrasound-guided acupotomy for plantar fasciitis and to evaluate its clinical efficacy and recurrence rate. Methods Patients diagnosed with plantar fasciitis in the Department of Orthopedics at the Second Affiliated Hospital of Wenzhou Medical University between January 2023 and December 2025 were selected. Those who met the inclusion criteria were randomly divided into a experimental group, n=48 and control group, n=47. Both groups received treatment once a week for two weeks. The Visual Analogue Score (VAS), American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) score, and plantar fascia thickness were assessed and analyzed before treatment, as well as at 1 week, 3 months, and 6 months after treatment. The clinical efficacy, recurrence rate and safety of the two methods were compared. Results (1) At 1 week, 3 months, and 6 months after treatment, both groups showed significantly lower VAS scores and plantar fascia thickness compared to before treatment, and significantly higher AOFAS scores (all P < 0.05). (2) At 3 and 6 months after treatment, the experimental group had lower VAS scores and plantar fascia thickness than the control group, and significantly higher AOFAS scores (all P < 0.05). (3) At 3 and 6 months after treatment, VAS scores in both groups were higher than those at 1 week after treatment, while plantar fascia thickness in the experimental group was further reduced compared to that at 1 week (all P < 0.05). (4) At 6 months after treatment, the VAS score in the control group was higher than that at 3 months, the plantar fascia thickness in the experimental group was greater than that at 3 months, and the AOFAS score in the experimental group was lower than that at 1 week (all P < 0.05). (5) The overall efficacy of the experimental group was superior to that of the control group (P < 0.05). (6)The recurrence rate in the experimental group was lower than that in the control group Conclusions Both acupotomy methods are effective in treating plantar fasciitis, but ultrasound-guided acupotomy provides better long-term pain control, functional improvement, higer recovery and higer safety., with lowe recurrence rate. Trial registration Chinese Clinical Trial Registry Number: ChiCTR2300074714.August 14th, 2023.

title: Intravitreal Methotrexate as a Prophylactic Strategy for Proliferative Vitreoretinopathy in High-Risk Retinal Detachment
abstract: Abstract Background Proliferative vitreoretinopathy (PVR) remains the major cause of surgical failure in rhegmatogenous retinal detachment (RRD). This study evaluates the anatomical and functional outcomes, as well as the safety, of a standardized intraoperative intravitreal methotrexate infusion protocol during pars plana vitrectomy (PPV) in eyes at risk of PVR (grade B) or with established PVR (grade C). Methods A retrospective cohort study was conducted on 60 consecutive eyes of 59 patients with RRD and PVR grade B (n = 29) or grade C (n = 31) undergoing PPV with adjunct intraoperative methotrexate between November 2024 and February 2026 at a german tertiary center. Methotrexate (40 mg) was administered via a 500 mL balanced salt solution infusion. Functional and structural testing included best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), intraocular pressure, multifocal electroretinogram, perimetry, and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography. The primary outcome measure was single-surgery anatomical success (SSAS) at 12 weeks after primary surgery or after silicone oil removal. Secondary outcomes included BCVA changes and complication rates. Results SSAS was achieved in 81.7% of all eyes, with a significantly higher success rate in eyes with PVR grade B compared to PVR grade C (93.1% versus 71.0%; p = 0.043). At 12 weeks, BCVA improved significantly in macula-off cases (p < 0.001) and remained stable in macula-on cases. Postoperative multifocal electroretinogram and perimetry confirmed preserved central retinal function. No ocular or systemic adverse events related to methotrexate occurred. Conclusions The standardized intraoperative intravitreal methotrexate infusion protocol is safe, feasible, and associated with high single-surgery reattachment rates, particularly in PVR grade B eyes. Anatomical outcomes in PVR grade C eyes were comparable to other complex PVR cohorts, without any drug-related local or systemic toxicity. Trial registration Not applicable (retrospective observational study).

title: Machine/Deep Learning-Based Position Prediction of Pulmonary Nodules in Free- Breathing CT-Guided Lung Puncture: A Single-Center Prospective Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background Cranio-caudal respiratory drift of pulmonary nodules severely compromises accuracy of free-breathing CT-guided thoracic interventions, contributing to repeated CT acquisitions, prolonged procedure time, elevated patient radiation burden, and higher complication risks of pneumothorax and pulmonary hemorrhage. Conventional motion mitigation approaches such as breath-holding and respiratory gating require high-level patient compliance and constrain needle insertion to narrow predefined respiratory phases, which limits real-world clinical utility. This work addresses this unmet clinical need by developing and validating novel real-time artificial-intelligence prediction models. Leveraging only one baseline planning CT together with low-cost, portable nasal airflow and respiratory inductive plethysmography (RIP) signals, our framework achieves sub-millimeter prediction of nodule cranio-caudal position without additional dynamic imaging. Methods This single-center prospective cohort enrolled 139 patients with 143 nodules undergoing pre-VATS CT microcoil localization. Synchronized respiratory waveforms, paired CT scans, clinical, lesion and procedural metadata were collected. Nodule vertical displacement was quantified via Z-axis coordinate shifts of each nodule’s maximum cross-section geometric center. In total, 2275 paired CT datasets were split 4:1:1 for model training, validation and independent testing. Prediction performance was quantified using mean squared error (MSE). Results The nasal-airflow-driven SVM yielded validation/test MSE values of 0.099/0.166 mm², versus 0.120/0.186 mm² for ResNet-18. RIP-based SVM achieved validation/test MSE of 0.100/0.168 mm² compared with 0.122/0.198 mm² for ResNet-18. Across heterogeneous breathing patterns and lesion locations, absolute prediction errors of central Z-coordinates remained below 0.5 mm for all constructed models. Conclusions Portable respiratory monitoring coupled with machine-learning enables sub-millimeter nodule Z-position prediction without mandatory breath-hold or phase-locked gating. This solution can be directly integrated into existing manual CT-guided puncture workflows to improve procedural safety and efficiency with minimal additional hardware; it also provides an essential technical building block for next-generation robotic thoracic interventional platforms. Trial registration: ChiCTR2300068696 (2023-02-27)

title: An integrative molecular tumor board approach to pediatric B atypical choroid plexus papilloma with an equivocal residual lesion: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Choroid plexus tumors are rare pediatric intracranial neoplasms comprising benign choroid plexus papilloma, atypical choroid plexus papilloma, and choroid plexus carcinoma. DNA methylation profiling refines risk stratification, distinguishing pediatric choroid plexus tumors into low-risk pediatric A and high-risk pediatric B subgroups, and may support treatment decisions when histology and clinical behavior are discordant. Case presentation A 2.6-year-old white boy from Germany presented with raised intracranial pressure from a large left lateral ventricular mass. Subtotal resection and second-look surgery left > 1.5 cm² residual tumor. Histopathology was discordant between choroid plexus papilloma and atypical choroid plexus papilloma, whereas methylation profiling confirmed a choroid plexus tumor of pediatric subgroup B; staging showed no dissemination. Because of young age and lower-grade appearance, close surveillance was chosen. At 3-month follow-up, local progression required two further resections, reducing residual tumor to < 1.5 cm². Histology then favored atypical papilloma bordering on carcinoma. Precision-oncology molecular analysis revealed no actionable target and broad chemoresistance. Individualized systemic chemotherapy was initiated, but further progression occurred, with a new enhancing lesion along the surgical tract. Subsequent resection achieved near-total removal, including the suspicious tract areas, and viable atypical papilloma was confirmed at the primary site and tract. Given the uncertain significance of minimal residual enhancement, further therapy was deferred. Approximately 30 months after diagnosis, the child remains in radiological remission. Conclusions This case highlights the diagnostic and therapeutic complexity of pediatric B atypical choroid plexus papilloma. Integrating histology, methylation profiling, precision-oncology results, repeated maximal safe resections, and individualized interdisciplinary decision-making achieved durable remission while limiting treatment-related morbidity.
