title: Multimodal imaging characterization of structural phenotypes and biomarkers in choroidal hemangioma associated with Sturge–Weber syndrome
abstract: Abstract Background To identify and characterize microstructural alterations and biomarkers of diffuse choroidal hemangioma (DCH) associated with Sturge–Weber syndrome (SWS) using multimodal imaging. Methods This was a retrospective, observational study where sixteen eyes of 16 patients with SWS and DCH underwent a comprehensive clinical evaluation and a standardized non-invasive multimodal imaging protocol, including color fundus photography, near-infrared reflectance (NIR) and infrared (IR) imaging, fundus autofluorescence, and spectral-domain optical coherence tomography (SDOCT). Microstructural alterations across the neurosensory retina, retinal pigment epithelium (RPE), and choriocapillaris were qualitatively graded by independent masked experts and correlated with choroidal subfoveal thickness (CSFT) and clinical parameters. Results Multimodal imaging identified four distinct microstructural phenotypes. The most frequent finding was hyperreflective dots, seen in 81.25% (13/16) of eyes as round-to-angular hyperreflective structures on NIR/IR imaging. Inner retinal folds appeared in 37.5% (6/16) of eyes as undulations and irregularities affecting the internal limiting membrane and retinal nerve fiber layer. Drusenoid-like lesions, characterized by granular hyperreflectivity localized between the ellipsoid zone and the RPE, resembling subretinal drusenoid deposits, were observed in 31.2% (5/16) of eyes. A demarcation line was seen as a linear or curved hyperreflective line on NIR in 18.75% (3/16) of eyes. Discussion DCH in SWS is characterized by a specific spectrum of secondary structural remodeling at the chorioretinal interface. These microstructural phenotypes likely reflect a combination of chronic mechanical strain from the underlying mass and localized tissue hypoxia due to an inefficient vascular environment, serving as valuable non-invasive biomarkers for tracking disease chronicity and monitoring disease progression.

Inner retinal folds appeared in 37.5% (6/16) of eyes as undulations and irregularities affecting the internal limiting membrane and retinal nerve fiber layer. Drusenoid-like lesions, characterized by granular hyperreflectivity localized between the ellipsoid zone and the RPE, resembling subretinal drusenoid deposits, were observed in 31.2% (5/16) of eyes. A demarcation line was seen as a linear or curved hyperreflective line on NIR in 18.75% (3/16) of eyes. Discussion DCH in SWS is characterized by a specific spectrum of secondary structural remodeling at the chorioretinal interface. These microstructural phenotypes likely reflect a combination of chronic mechanical strain from the underlying mass and localized tissue hypoxia due to an inefficient vascular environment, serving as valuable non-invasive biomarkers for tracking disease chronicity and monitoring disease progression.

title: Muscle fibre-resolved spatial transcriptomics of regeneration, necrosis and border zones in human paraspinal muscle
abstract: Abstract Focal necrotizing lesion fields in human skeletal muscle contain a mosaic of necrotic fibres, regenerative fibres, and morphologically preserved neighbouring fibres, but their fibre-resolved molecular organisation remains poorly defined. We applied targeted Xenium spatial transcriptomics to a human lumbar paraspinal muscle biopsy with toxic myopathy and integrated the analysis with serial post-run hematoxylin and eosin stain, adult and neonatal myosin heavy-chain isoforms, immunostaining for membrane attack complex of complement (C5b9) and manual fibre-level region-of-interest segmentation. Distant normal type 1 and type 2 fibres, necrotic fibres, regenerative fibres, and intact type 1 and type 2 fibres immediately adjacent to necrosis or regeneration were compared. Baseline transcriptional differences between distant normal type 1 and type 2 fibres were modest, whereas lesion-associated contrasts were substantially broader, indicating that pathological state outweighed basal fibre identity within this targeted panel. Necrotic fibre regions were enriched for immune/myeloid-associated transcripts, including PLA2G7 , TREM2 , FCGR3A , MS4A4A , CD163 , MRC1 , and PTPRC , whereas regenerative fibres preferentially expressed structural and calcium-handling genes, including MYBPC1 , DES , MEF2C , S100A1 , and PVALB . Despite preserved morphology, fibres bordering necrosis displayed a pronounced border-zone signature that largely overlapped the necrotic programme, whereas neighbourhood effects around regeneration were weaker and fibre-type dependent. These findings define necrosis, regeneration, and their border zones as distinct spatial states within a focal human muscle lesion and indicate that fibres adjacent to necrosis, despite being morphologically normal, are unsuitable internal comparators.

title: Clinicopathological Features and Prognosis of Acute Interstitial Nephritis: A Study of 26 Patients
abstract: Abstract Objective : Acute interstitial nephritis (AIN) is an acute kidney injury (AKI) characterized by renal interstitial inflammation and tubular damage. This study aims to clarify its clinical features, etiologies, and prognosis. Methods: Clinical data from 26 AIN patients were retrospectively analyzed, including demographics, manifestations, lab tests, ultrasound, pathology, etiology, and outcomes. Results: Mean age was 54.8 years, with 53.8% aged 51–70 years. Females accounted for 61.5% (M:F=1:1.6). Hypertension (42.3%) and diabetes (19.2%) were common comorbidities. Digestive symptoms (38.5%) were the most frequent presentation. AKI occurred in 88.5%, all stage 3, and 38.5% received short-term hemodialysis. Lab findings showed elevated creatinine, BUN, and uric acid, with mild anemia in some. Renal ultrasound revealed increased cortical echogenicity (42.3%) and cysts (23.0%). Biopsy demonstrated interstitial inflammatory infiltration (mainly lymphocytes) in all cases, and 76.9% had interstitial fibrosis. Drug-related causes accounted for 30.8%, while 30.8% remained unknown. Eighteen patients received glucocorticoids. After 3 months, 22 patients were followed up, with a renal recovery rate of 95.5%. Conclusion: AIN is more common in middle-aged and elderly women, with drugs being a major causative factor. It typically presents as severe AKI. Renal biopsy reveals characteristic interstitial inflammation. With active treatment, the overall prognosis is favorable. Emphasis should be placed on preventing and early identifying drug-induced kidney injury.

title: Individualized Brain Morphometry Through User-Controlled Normative Database
abstract: Abstract Identifying structural abnormalities such as hippocampal sclerosis (HS) and focal cortical dysplasia (FCD) on conventional magnetic resonance imaging remains challenging. We introduce the Single-Subject Morphometry (SSM) toolbox, a voxel-based framework designed with rule-based statistical approaches for individualized morphometric analysis with customizable embedded normative metrics. SSM utilizes conventional preprocessing pipelines to generate subject-specific maps and reports of gray (GM) and white matter abnormalities and FCD lesions. We evaluated SSM against reference tools using 377 subjects from public and internal datasets for the GM and FCD modalities. For HS (n = 211), SSM achieved a lateralization accuracy of 94% while AID-HS achieved 96%. For FCD detection (n = 103), SSM correctly localized lesions in 70% of cases, similar to the 73% achieved by MELD-Graph, while completing processing approximately nine times faster. Although SSM yielded more false-positive clusters, it provided robust whole-brain statistical inference rather than restricted focal predictions. The SSM toolbox provides a flexible, fast, and statistically interpretable framework for individualized morphometric analysis. By enabling comprehensive whole-brain characterization of structural abnormalities, SSM offers a valuable and transparent alternative for clinical research and diagnostic support in neurological disorders.

title: Neurofibromatosis Type 1 Complicated by Moyamoya Syndrome with Secondary Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Objective： To analyze the clinical characteristics and pathogenesis of spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage secondary to neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1)-associated moyamoya syndrome (MMS), and summarize standardized diagnosis and individualized surgical strategies for this rare comorbidity. Methods： The clinical, pathological, imaging and follow-up data of one 42-year-old female patient with NF1 combined with bilateral moyamoya syndrome and basal ganglia hemorrhage admitted in August 2025 were retrospectively collected. Relevant domestic and international literatures were systematically reviewed to summarize the clinical features and treatment principles of this disease. Results： The patient had lifelong typical NF1 cutaneous lesions without traditional cerebrovascular risk factors. Emergency CT revealed massive basal ganglia hemorrhage with mass effect and cerebral hernia risk. MRA confirmed bilateral distal internal carotid artery occlusion and typical moyamoya vascular network. Subcutaneous tumor pathology and immunohistochemistry verified benign neurofibroma. She received emergency hematoma evacuation plus decompressive craniectomy, followed by cranioplasty later. Three-month follow-up CT showed complete hematoma absorption, and the patient achieved favorable neurological recovery. Conclusion： NF1-related moyamoya syndrome should be suspected in middle-aged patients with unexplained intracerebral hemorrhage. Staged surgical management including emergency decompression and subsequent cerebral revascularization can effectively reduce the risk of recurrent stroke. Long-term multidisciplinary follow-up is required for genetic counseling and vascular monitoring.

title: Brain Structural Changes Underlying Dysphagia in Parkinson’s Disease: An Exploratory Multimodal Quantitative MRI Study
abstract: Abstract Dysphagia is a substantial and often underrecognized burden in Parkinson’s disease (PD), and its neural underpinnings remain poorly understood. In this retrospective study, we employed a multimodal neuroimaging approach to investigate structural brain changes associated with dysphagia in PD. We included 105 participants in the age range of 45 to 84 years: 35 PD with dysphagia (PDD), 35 PD without dysphagia (PDnD), and 35 age- and sex-matched healthy controls (HC). Oropharyngeal dysphagia was confirmed through clinical swallowing evaluation or video fluoroscopic swallow study. We obtained T1 and diffusion-weighted MRI from all our participants. We analyzed them using voxel-based morphometry, surface-based morphometry, tract-based spatial statistics, and graph-theoretical structural connectivity analysis. Relative to HC and PDnD groups, the PDD group showed widespread gray matter atrophy ( p < .05) in the cerebellum, temporal lobes, subcortical regions, and prefrontal cortices. Surface-based morphometry revealed significant cortical thinning ( p < .00001), reduced sulcal depth, altered fractal dimension, and increased gyrification (all p < .05) in motor, limbic, and orbitofrontal regions. The PDD group also showed significant white matter atrophy in brainstem, cerebral, and cerebellar areas, with reduced fractional anisotropy and increased mean diffusivity in key sensorimotor and autonomic pathways ( p < .05). No widespread differences were observed between the PDD and PDnD groups across structural modalities. Graph-theoretical analysis showed trends toward reduced global network integration and segregation in the PDD group, though these did not reach statistical significance. Together, these findings support a model in which dysphagia in PD reflects widespread, network-level structural degeneration across both gray and white matter, extending beyond classical brainstem swallowing centers.

title: Treatment outcomes of a combination with intensity-modulated radiotherapy and three fractions of computed tomography-guided brachytherapy for uterine cervical cancer: A single-institution analysis in Japan
abstract: Abstract Background To evaluate the midterm treatment outcomes, efficacy, and safety of a radiotherapy (RT) regimen combining intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and a reduced three-fraction schedule of computed tomography (CT)-guided brachytherapy (BT) for uterine cervical cancer (UCC). Methods This retrospective study evaluated patients with UCC (International Federation of Gynecology and Obstetrics 2018 stages IB–IVB) treated at our institution between May 2017 and December 2023. The patients received whole-pelvic IMRT (45–50.4 Gy) with an adjustable boost for enlarged lymph nodes followed by 3 fractions of CT-guided high-dose-rate BT. The primary endpoint was the local control (LC) rate; the secondary endpoints were disease-free survival (DFS), overall survival (OS), and late toxicities. Results A total of 92 patients were included, and 77 patients received platinum-based concurrent chemotherapy. The median follow-up period was 43.5 months. The median total high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) D90 dose was 77.1 Gy. The 3-year LC, DFS, and OS rates were 94.5%, 66.5%, and 86.2%, respectively. T stage was an independent prognostic factor for both LC and DFS, whereas T stage and HR-CTV at initial BT were independent prognostic factors for OS. Grade ≥ 3 late toxicities were observed in 4 patients (4.3%). Conclusions The combination of IMRT and a reduced 3-fraction CT-guided BT achieves good LC with acceptable toxicity in patients with stage IB–IVB UCC. This regimen offers a reasonable and practical approach to minimize patients’ physical and psychological burden, although a more intense treatment should be considered for patients with advanced-stage disease.

title: Molecular Diagnosis and Pathway Convergence in Neurodevelopmental Disorders: An Integrative Genomic Study of 1,011 Patients
abstract: Abstract Background Genetic factors are critical to diagnosing neurodevelopmental disorders (NDDs). Despite advances in genetic diagnostics, a considerable proportion of patients remain undiagnosed, highlighting the urgent need to identify underlying genetic etiologies and discover additional pathogenic genes and molecular mechanisms. Method Whole-exome sequencing (WES), trio-WES, panel sequencing, chromosomal microarray analysis (CMA), or multiplex ligation-dependent probe amplification (MLPA) were used for identifying potential variant. Comprehensive clinical and laboratory data were collected. All patients were classified into 18 phenotypic subgroups. GWAS was conducted for sequencing-negative cases. Results Of the 1011 patients with GDD/ID, the most comorbid symptoms were abnormal MRI findings, craniofacial malformations, and malnutrition/feeding difficulties/growth retardation. The overall diagnostic rate was 54% (508/940), with 343(36.5%) single-nucleotide variations (SNVs) and 157(16.7%) Copy number variants (CNVs). Among SNV-positive cases, we identified 166/430(38.6% ) novel variants and 179/430 (41.6%) de novo variants. In CNV-positive cases, the top recurrent cytobands were 15q11.2-q13.1, Xq28, and 7q11.2. GWAS analysis showed that genetically negative cases were significant enrichment in the Rap1 signaling and O-glycosylation modification, while positive cases significantly enriched in axonogenesis and chromatin remodeling. Integrated analysis of two sets highlighted convergence on O-glycosylation and calcium response. Protein-protein interaction analysis of 47 overlapping genes identified the RAS-MAPK signaling pathway. Conclusion: Our findings further supported the clinical value of trio-WES/WES as a first-tier diagnostic strategy for NDDs. Importantly, O-glycosylation modification emerges as a critical molecular mechanism in NDDs, offering a potential convergence may reveal common neurobiological processes.

title: Deep Learning Reconstruction in Pediatric Knee MRI: Evaluation of Image Quality, Reader Preference, and Acquisition Time
abstract: Abstract Background Deep learning–based reconstruction can accelerate MR image acquisition while potentially preserving image quality. Faster imaging is particularly helpful in pediatric patients, who may be more susceptible to motion-related degradation during prolonged examinations. Objective To compare image quality, reader preference, and acquisition time between Deep Resolve–accelerated and conventional turbo spin-echo (TSE) sequences in pediatric knee MRI and to assess inter-reader agreement for the detection of knee abnormalities. Materials and methods This retrospective, institutional review board–approved study included pediatric patients who underwent clinical knee MRI with both conventional and Deep Resolve–accelerated TSE sequences. Two pediatric radiologists independently evaluated the paired image sets for overall image quality, contrast resolution, motion, artifacts, diagnostic confidence, and delineation of bone, articular cartilage, ligaments, and tendons. Reader preference and qualitative image-quality assessments between accelerated and conventional sequences were compared. Inter-reader agreement for detection of knee abnormalities was assessed, and acquisition times were compared. Results Eighty-five paired sequences from 60 patients were included (mean age, 14.2 years; SD, 2.4 years). Deep Resolve was preferred over conventional imaging in 96.2% of Reader 1 assessments and 96.4% of Reader 2 assessments. Deep Resolve received the highest overall image-quality score in 92.5% and 96.4% of assessments, respectively, compared with 17.5% and 14.5% for conventional images. Overall image-quality scores were significantly higher for DRB than for conventional imaging for both readers (both P < 0.001). Interreader agreement for abnormality detection was excellent (97.6% agreement; kappa, 0.934; 95% CI, 0.838–1.000). Deep Resolve–accelerated sequences reduced acquisition time by approximately 50% to 77% across sequence types. Conclusion Deep Resolve–accelerated TSE sequences substantially reduced acquisition time and were strongly preferred by both readers for image quality and contrast resolution. Interreader agreement for abnormality detection was excellent, supporting deep learning–accelerated reconstruction as a practical approach to shortening pediatric knee MRI examinations while preserving diagnostic assessment.

title: Subdural Empyema as the Presenting Feature of a Cerebral Aneurysm in a Pediatric Patient in the Intensive Care Unit of a Teaching Hospital in Maputo, Mozambique: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Cerebral aneurysms are rare in pediatric populations, accounting for less than 5% of all aneurysms. Etiologies are often congenital or infectious. To date, no cases of pediatric cerebral aneurysms have been reported in Mozambique. Case Presentation: We report the first documented case of a pediatric cerebral aneurysm in Mozambique. A 13-year-old boy was admitted to the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) with a five-day history of sudden severe headache, fever, and right-sided focal seizures. Imaging revealed a right frontal parafalcine subdural empyema, which was surgically drained. Although the patient initially improved, he was readmitted 15 days later with a sudden loss of consciousness and generalized seizures. Encephalic Computed Tomography and angiography revealed intraventricular hemorrhage and ruptured aneurysms of the pericallosal and right middle cerebral arteries. Neurosurgical intervention was not available; The blood culture isolated Staphylococcus aureus , and broad-spectrum was considered, as well as supportive care, and the patient survived with neurological sequelae. Discussion This case highlights a rare and severe presentation of pediatric cerebral aneurysm associated with subdural empyema of likely infectious etiology. The vascular territories affected were atypical, and diagnosis was delayed due to the condition's rarity and limited resources. Conclusion Despite being rare, cerebral aneurysms in children should be considered in cases of neurological deterioration, especially with signs of intracranial infection. Early neuroimaging and timely neurosurgical care are essential for better outcomes in resource-limited settings.

title: Pretreatment IVIM histogram parameters using multiple ROI strategies for predicting treatment response and survival outcomes in locally advanced rectal cancer
abstract: Abstract Purpose To evaluate pretreatment intravoxel incoherent motion diffusion-weighted imaging (IVIM)-derived histogram and percentile parameters obtained using different regions of interest (ROI) delineation strategies for predicting tumor regression grade (TRG), pathological complete response (pCR) and survival outcomes in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer (LARC). Materials and methods A total of 113 patients with LARC who underwent pretreatment IVIM were retrospectively enrolled. Histogram and percentile parameters of the true diffusion coefficient (D), pseudo-diffusion coefficient (D*), and perfusion fraction ( f ) were extracted using three ROI delineation strategies, including whole-tumor volume ROI (ROI WTV ), single-slice ROI (ROI SS ), and reader-defined small-sample ROI (ROI RDSS ). Patients were divided into good responders (TRG 0–1) and poor responders (TRG 2–3). Predictive models were constructed using LASSO and multivariate logistic regression. The area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) was used to evaluate the predictive performance. Survival outcomes were evaluated using Kaplan–Meier analysis. title: CNV Based Genetic Risk Score for Aortic Aneurysm
abstract: Abstract Ultrasound screening guidelines for Aortic Aneurysm (AA) miss many at-risk individuals, including women, younger men, and non-smokers. We investigated whether genome-wide structural descriptors derived from microarray Log R-Ratio (LRR) data could provide a non-invasive genetic risk score to triage patients who fall outside standard screening criteria. We analyzed microarray LRR data from 933 AA cases and 5,083 healthy elderly controls (84 years or older) in the All of Us Research Program, computing 512 moment descriptors across 128 genomic windows. A Generalized Linear Model (GLM) achieved the highest generalization performance on an independent, covariate-matched held-out cohort (AUC = 0.645, 95% CI: 0.590 to 0.697). Permutation testing confirmed that GLM accuracy relied on genome-wide covariance patterns (p < 0.0001). As a rule-out triage tool, the GLM achieved 27.9% specificity at 90.1% sensitivity, correctly excluding 63 of 226 healthy controls while capturing 128 of 142 cases.

title: Natural Language Processing and Large Language Model-Based Automated AO/OTA Classification of Proximal Femoral Fractures: A MIMIC-IV Retrospective Study
abstract: Abstract Background Accurate AO/OTA classification of proximal femoral fractures is a critical step in surgical decision-making and prognostic evaluation; however, the complexity of the classification system and the heterogeneity of terminology in radiology reports pose significant challenges for large-scale, standardized application of the classification. In recent years, with the advancement of AI technologies, large language models (LLMs) equipped with retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) capabilities have offered new possibilities for automatically extracting fracture classification information from unstructured radiology reports. Methods This study conducted a retrospective analysis of 23,179 radiology reports from the MIMIC-IV database. Through a multi-stage annotation process involving independent labeling by two orthopedic surgeons and adjudication by a senior expert, a total of 157 acute cases of AO/OTA type 31A (intertrochanteric fractures) and type 31B (femoral neck fractures) were ultimately included. We evaluated three experimental models: zero‑shot prompting, few‑shot learning (5 examples per class), and RAG‑augmented prompting (incorporating a structured AO classification knowledge base). Classification performance was assessed using accuracy, F1‑score, and confusion matrices. All type 31C (femoral head fractures) cases underwent expert re‑adjudication to evaluate annotation quality. Results The RAG‑LLM framework achieved an accuracy of 94.29% (F1 = 94.29%) in distinguishing 31A from 31B fractures on a balanced test set of 70 cases (35 each of 31A and 31B). Zero‑shot prompting attained the same accuracy (94.29%, F1 = 94.28%), while few‑shot learning unexpectedly dropped to 88.57% (F1 = 88.53%). Confusion matrices showed minimal misclassifications: 2/35 cases of 31A were misclassified as 31B, and 2/35 cases of 31B were misclassified as 31A. A key finding was that after expert re‑adjudication of 47 cases initially labeled as 31C, only 6 (12.8%) met the true AO/OTA 31C criteria; the remaining 41 (87.2%) were actually acetabular fractures (AO/OTA type 61) or misclassified 31A/31B cases. The subtype classification for 31B fractures (31B1 vs. 31B2) achieved an accuracy of 70.59%, reflecting the inherent difficulty of text‑based subtype differentiation. Conclusion The RAG‑LLM demonstrated excellent performance in binary classification of AO/OTA 31A versus 31B proximal femoral fractures using real‑world radiology reports. The systematic bias found in 31C labeling within MIMIC‑IV highlights the critical importance of expert data quality assurance in real‑world evidence studies. The comparable performance between zero‑shot and RAG models suggests that modern LLMs already possess inherent knowledge of AO/OTA classification, though RAG may offer advantages in more nuanced tasks. These findings support the potential of LLM‑assisted workflows to streamline fracture classification in clinical and research settings.

title: Ultrasound-measured abdominal fat thickness: A diagnostic marker for metabolic syndrome and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease in children and adolescents with obesity
abstract: Abstract Objective The increasing incidence of metabolic syndrome (MetS) and Metabolic Dysfunction-Associated Steatotic Liver Disease (MASLD) among children with obesity underscores the need to identify early, non-invasive biomarkers. Despite the extensive research on visceral fat, the predictive value of ultrasonographic subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) has received comparatively less attention. The present study evaluates the clinical utility of SAT as a diagnostic indicator in pediatric obesity. Methods The study prospectively evaluated children aged 7–18 years, including 61 obese patients and 41 controls. The diagnosis of MetS was made using modified WHO criteria. Abdominal Wall Fat Thickness (AWFT) was measured by a linear probe at the umbilical level, and hepatic steatosis was graded semi-quantitatively. The diagnostic accuracy was evaluated using ROC curves and logistic regression. Results This study demonstrated a significant correlation between AWFT and MetS as well as the severity of hepatic steatosis (p < 0.001). The optimal AWFT threshold for discriminating MetS was established at > 2.7 cm, which was associated with a 2.6-fold increased risk in the adjusted analysis (sensitivity: 75%, specificity: 66%, PPV: 60%, and NPV: 81%). Conclusion AWFT is a non-invasive, readily accessible ultrasonographic biomarker for MetS in children with obesity. Our findings suggest that incorporating an AWFT threshold of > 2.7 cm into routine pediatric obesity assessments could facilitate early identification of high-risk individuals and promote targeted intervention strategies.

title: Elevated S100B Levels Are Associated with Early Coagulation Disturbances in the Prehospital Phase of Severe Traumatic Brain Injury: An Experimental Pilot Study
abstract: Abstract Background Trauma-induced coagulopathy (TIC) following severe traumatic brain injury (sTBI) substantially contributes to secondary intracranial haemorrhage and mortality. sTBI confirmed by elevated blood-based neurobiomarkers, including S100B is associated with functional and dynamic coagulation abnormalities. Previous studies demonstrated that thromboelastometry-guided haemostatic management showed benefits through in-hospital management of trauma-associated intracranial bleedings; however, the initial stages of TIC in the prehospital phase remain insufficiently characterised. We hypothesized that the selective coagulation factor deficiency underlying sTBI-associated coagulopathy, potentially amplified by immune-mediated proinflammatory mechanisms, could be identified already in the prehospital phase. Methods A multicenter prospective observational study was conducted at three prehospital ambulance stations in Hungary. Adult patients with suspected sTBI, based on the overall prehospital clinical presentation — including GCS ≤8, suspected intracranial hemorrhage and/or the need for intensive care — were included. Prehospital blood samples were obtained prior to tranexamic acid administration for thromboelastometry (ROTEM ® ) and measurement of serum total calcium, S100B, and IL-6 concentrations. Results From the rotational thromboelastometry parameters FIBTEM A5 fell below the critical threshold of 9 mm in 7 of 12 patients (58.3%), with a median of 8 mm (IQR: 5.8–10.0 mm), indicating impaired fibrinogen-dependent clot formation. EXTEM clotting time exceeded the upper reference limit in 3 of 13 patients (23.1%). The median EXTEM A5 was 41 mm (IQR: 36–46), at the lower reference limit. Serum S100B concentrations were markedly elevated (median: 4.84 μg/L, IQR: 1.88–9.56) and correlated significantly with Marshall CT classification (r = 0.706, p = 0.010). The total serum calcium concentration trended towards the lower limit of the reference range (median: 2.26 mmol/L, IQR: 2.20–2.31). IL-6 levels were markedly elevated (median: 22.9 pg/mL, IQR: 6.2–65.3) and did not significantly correlate with EXTEM clotting time (r = 0.51, p = 0.074). Conclusions Selective fibrinogen-dependent coagulation impairment is detectable in the hyperacute prehospital phase of sTBI, prior to any resuscitative intervention, and may be linked to an early immune-mediated proinflammatory response. These findings support early prehospital fibrinogen supplementation and tranexamic acid therapy. The marked prehospital elevation of S100B, which correlates with intracranial injury severity, confirms its value as an early diagnostic biomarker of sTBI. Trial registration : Not applicable.

title: Evaluating Medical Visual Question Answering for Telemedicine: A Secondary Data Review and the TRACE-MedVQA Framework
abstract: Abstract Medical visual question answering (Med-VQA) combines medical image understanding and natural-language processing to answer clinically relevant questions about radiographs, computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, pathology, and other visual data. This study evaluates existing Med-VQA methods from secondary sources and proposes a telemedicine-oriented framework. A qualitative comparative review was conducted across benchmark datasets, task-specific convolutional and transformer models, domain-adapted vision-language encoders, and recent generative large multimodal models. The evidence shows a clear progression from closed-set classification toward open-ended generation, but clinical deployment remains restricted by small and imbalanced datasets, weak external validation, hallucination risk, limited uncertainty reporting, and insufficient visual grounding. To address these limitations, the study proposes TRACE-MedVQA, a Telemedicine-Ready, Retrieval-Augmented, Calibrated, and Explainable framework. It combines modality-aware image encoding, clinical question encoding, cross-modal attention, trusted knowledge retrieval, dual answer routing, confidence calibration, abstention, visual explanation, and clinician oversight. The framework offers a practical research direction for safer remote decision support while preserving human responsibility.

title: Longitudinal Clinical and MRI Changes Suggestive of Subclinical Disease Progression in Egyptian Patients with Relapsing-Remitting Multiple Sclerosis: A Prospective Observational Study
abstract: Abstract Background Progression independent of relapse activity (PIRA) is increasingly recognized as a major contributor to disability accumulation in relapsing-remitting multiple sclerosis (RRMS), reflecting ongoing neurodegeneration despite apparent control of inflammatory disease activity. However, longitudinal data integrating comprehensive clinical assessment with quantitative MRI biomarkers remain limited, particularly in North African populations. Methods This prospective observational cohort study included 50 patients with RRMS. Assessments at baseline, 6, and 12 months included the Expanded Disability Status Scale (EDSS), Symbol Digit Modalities Test (SDMT), Nine-Hole Peg Test (9-HPT), Timed 25-Foot Walk Test (T25-FWT), and Arabic Modified Fatigue Impact Scale (A-MFIS). Quantitative brain MRI, including regional volumetric analysis, cortical thickness measurements, and white matter lesion assessment, was performed at baseline and after one year. Results During the one-year follow-up, significant deterioration was observed in disability, cognitive performance, upper-limb function, and fatigue, whereas walking performance remained relatively stable. Clinically meaningful cognitive decline (≥ 4-point reduction in SDMT score) occurred in 24% of patients after 6 months and in 44% after one year. EDSS worsening was observed in eight patients at 6 months and seven patients at one year, including progression in 10.3% of patients without documented relapse during the second follow-up period. Quantitative MRI demonstrated significant longitudinal changes in multiple cortical and subcortical brain regions despite stable white matter lesion burden, and clinical deterioration was associated with regional brain volumetric alterations involving the thalamus, cortical and total gray matter, cerebellum, and temporal structures. Older age, longer disease duration, greater relapse burden, and delayed initiation of disease-modifying therapy (DMT) were associated with less favorable clinical outcomes and greater brain atrophy, whereas higher educational attainment and monosymptomatic disease onset were associated with better longitudinal cognitive performance. Conclusion One-year longitudinal follow-up demonstrated measurable changes across multiple clinical domains and regional brain structures consistent with early subclinical disease progression in RRMS despite limited inflammatory activity. Quantitative MRI combined with sensitive cognitive and functional assessments detected changes beyond those captured by conventional disability measures, supporting their complementary role in monitoring early neurodegenerative progression.

title: Photon-Counting Computed Tomography Improves Interobserver Agreement in the Evaluation of Failed Stapes Surgery
abstract: Abstract Purpose Failed stapes surgery presents a diagnostic challenge requiring high-resolution imaging to guide revision. Energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT) is widely used but limited by spatial resolution and metal artifact. Photon-counting CT (PCCT) offers improved spatial resolution and reduced noise, with potential advantages in temporal bone imaging. The purpose of this study was to compare PCCT and EID-CT in identifying etiologies of failed primary stapes surgery, with emphasis on diagnostic accuracy, interobserver agreement, and interpreter confidence Methods In this retrospective study, 38 patients with failed primary stapes surgery who underwent successful revision surgery and pre-revision CT were included; 18 underwent PCCT and 20 underwent EID-CT. Three expert reviewers independently determined the cause of surgical failure, compared against the reference standard of intraoperative findings at revision. Diagnostic accuracy, interobserver agreement (Fleiss kappa), and reader confidence were compared between modalities. Results Overall interobserver agreement was substantially higher with PCCT (κ = 0.75; 95% CI, 0.60–0.90) than EID-CT (κ = 0.44; 95% CI, 0.30–0.59), with improved agreement observed across etiologies of failure; confidence intervals were non-overlapping for overall agreement and ossicular discontinuity. Consensus diagnostic accuracy was comparable between modalities (88.9% PCCT vs 85% EID-CT; p = 1.00), as was interpreter confidence (4.33 PCCT vs 4.17 EID-CT; p = 0.29). Conclusion In this small cohort, PCCT and EID-CT demonstrated similar diagnostic accuracy and reader confidence, whereas PCCT demonstrated significantly higher interobserver agreement, suggesting more reproducible assessment of failed stapes surgery and a potential role in supporting revision surgical planning.

title: A Novel Classification of Pediatric Medial Humeral Epicondyle Fractures Based on Elbow Stability and Analysis of Treatment Outcomes
abstract: Abstract Background: Fractures of the medial humeral epicondyle are common in children, yet existing classification systems are based on radiographic displacement, which has demonstrated poor interobserver reliability and fails to account for elbow stability—a key determinant of treatment and prognosis. This study proposes a novel stability-based classification system (K-L classification) for pediatric medial humeral epicondyle fractures, evaluates its clinical utility, and compares outcomes with those of the traditional Papavasiliou classification. Methods: A retrospective review was conducted on 447 pediatric patients with medial humeral epicondyle fractures treated at our institution between January 2018 and August 2025. Of these, 184 patients were classified and treated according to the traditional Papavasiliou classification. The remaining 263 patients were classified using the novel K-L classification, which was based on magnetic resonance imaging findings and physical examination (including valgus stress test and moving valgus stress test) to assess elbow stability and associated injuries. Treatment strategies were assigned according to each classification system. All patients were followed for a minimum of 12 months. Outcomes included the Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS), the excellent-and-good rate of MEPS, and complication rates, which were compared between the two classification groups. Results: In the Papavasiliou group (n=184), there were 14 type I, 69 type II, 65 type III, and 36 type IV fractures. Nonoperative treatment was administered to type I fractures and 23 type II fractures; operative treatment was performed on the remaining 46 type II fractures and all type III and type IV fractures. In the K-L group (n=263), there were 9 type I, 7 type IIa, 131 type IIb, 41 type IIIa, and 75 type IIIb fractures. Types I and IIa were treated nonoperatively, while types IIb, IIIa, and IIIb underwent operative treatment. At final follow-up, the mean MEPS was significantly higher in the K-L group than in the Papavasiliou group (94.16 ± 6.15 vs. 90.22 ± 8.03, P < 0.05). The excellent-and-good rate of MEPS was also significantly higher in the K-L group (100%, 263/263) compared with the Papavasiliou group (96.2%, 177/184) (P < 0.05). The overall complication rate was significantly lower in the K-L group (7.22%, 19/263) than in the Papavasiliou group (25.54%, 47/184) (P < 0.05). Conclusions: The novel K-L classification, which is based on elbow stability, provides a reliable and reproducible framework for guiding treatment decisions in pediatric medial humeral epicondyle fractures. It is associated with superior functional outcomes and a lower complication rate compared with the traditional displacement-based Papavasiliou classification. This system offers a practical and evidence-based approach to individualized management of these injuries.

The remaining 263 patients were classified using the novel K-L classification, which was based on magnetic resonance imaging findings and physical examination (including valgus stress test and moving valgus stress test) to assess elbow stability and associated injuries. Treatment strategies were assigned according to each classification system. All patients were followed for a minimum of 12 months. Outcomes included the Mayo Elbow Performance Score (MEPS), the excellent-and-good rate of MEPS, and complication rates, which were compared between the two classification groups. Results: In the Papavasiliou group (n=184), there were 14 type I, 69 type II, 65 type III, and 36 type IV fractures. Nonoperative treatment was administered to type I fractures and 23 type II fractures; operative treatment was performed on the remaining 46 type II fractures and all type III and type IV fractures. In the K-L group (n=263), there were 9 type I, 7 type IIa, 131 type IIb, 41 type IIIa, and 75 type IIIb fractures. Types I and IIa were treated nonoperatively, while types IIb, IIIa, and IIIb underwent operative treatment. At final follow-up, the mean MEPS was significantly higher in the K-L group than in the Papavasiliou group (94.16 ± 6.15 vs. 90.22 ± 8.03, P < 0.05). The excellent-and-good rate of MEPS was also significantly higher in the K-L group (100%, 263/263) compared with the Papavasiliou group (96.2%, 177/184) (P < 0.05). The overall complication rate was significantly lower in the K-L group (7.22%, 19/263) than in the Papavasiliou group (25.54%, 47/184) (P < 0.05). Conclusions: The novel K-L classification, which is based on elbow stability, provides a reliable and reproducible framework for guiding treatment decisions in pediatric medial humeral epicondyle fractures. It is associated with superior functional outcomes and a lower complication rate compared with the traditional displacement-based Papavasiliou classification. This system offers a practical and evidence-based approach to individualized management of these injuries.

title: Single‑port endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy combined with prosthesis breast reconstruction in breast cancer: a retrospective single-center study of 167 cases
abstract: Abstract Background Single‑port endoscopic nipple-sparing mastectomy combined with prosthetic breast reconstruction (E-NSM-PBR) has been used for breast repair due to aesthetic considerations. However, the clinical feasibility, postoperative complications and oncological safety of E-NSM-PBR in breast surgery remain controversial. This study presents our experience with the application of E-NSM-PBR in breast cancer patients and reports the preliminary results. Methods This is a retrospective study of 167 patients who underwent breast surgery using E-NSM-PBR at our institution between March 1, 2023 and December 31, 2024. Their clinicopathological characteristics, postoperative complications, cosmetic outcomes, and oncologic outcomes were analyzed. Results All patients underwent nipple-sparing mastectomy under single-port endoscopy, followed by breast prosthesis reconstruction. The average duration of unilateral surgery is 222.9 minutes (ranging from 115 to 537 minutes). The average operation time on both sides was 371 minutes (ranging from 348 to 390 minutes). The average reconstruction volume was 253.6 ml (ranging from 100 to 445 ml). The overall complication rate was 16.8%. The subcutaneous fluid and infection in the breast area are the most common complications in breast reconstruction, with a total of 18 cases (10.2%). The combined necrosis rate of the nipple-areola complex (NAC) and skin flaps is 3.6%. There were 3 cases of implant loss after postoperative radiotherapy. The incidence of bleeding complications was the lowest, only 1.2%. Cosmetic outcomes were satisfactory in 94.6% of patients on a four-point scale by three-panel assessment and 95.8% using the BCCT.core software. After a median follow-up of 29 months, one local and one systemic recurrence were observed. Conclusions E-NSM-PBR is a safe and feasible immediate breast reconstruction technique with concealed surgical incision and promising oncologic safety. For suitable candidates, E-NSM-PBR technology can provide good cosmetic results.

title: Epithelioid Haemangioendothelioma of the Gastric Wall with Unique Histomorphology: A Case Report
abstract: Abstract Background Epithelioid haemangioendothelioma (EHE) is an ultra-rare vascular neoplasm, characterized by local aggressiveness and metastatic potential. We report a case of primary gastric wall EHE in a 64-year-old man, detected incidentally on imaging. Case presentation: Contrast-enhanced CT revealed a well-circumscribed 18×19×14.5 mm mass arising from the gastric serosa with mild enhancement. Laparoscopic excision was performed. Histology demonstrated a heterogeneous tumour composed of cords, strands or small nests of endothelial and spindle cells with abundant eosinophilic cytoplasm embedded in a myxohyaline stroma. Immunohistochemistry (IHC) stain shows the neoplastic cells were negative for keratins, CD117, DOG1, S100, Desmin, HMB45, and STAT6, but diffuse positive for the endothelial marker CD34, focally positive for SMA, with a low Ki-67 proliferation index (~ 3%). The initial diagnosis was a low-grade mesenchymal neoplasm. On referral to a specialist center, additional IHC revealed strong nuclear TFE3 expression and absence of CAMTA1 and FLI1. These findings were highly suggestive of a YAP1-TFE3 rearranged epithelioid haemangioendothelioma. Although molecular confirmation was not performed in this case, the immune profile and histomorphology strongly supported this diagnosis. Conclusions This case highlights the importance of considering EHE in the differential diagnosis of gastric mesenchymal tumors and underscores the utility of TFE3 and CAMTA1 immunohistochemistry in guiding further diagnostic workup, particularly when molecular testing is unavailable.

title: Demographic shortcuts as marker-free backdoors: silent subgroup underdiagnosis that only operating-point audits detect
abstract: Abstract Medical imaging models read race and sex from pixels alone, making demographic identity a usable backdoor trigger. Flipping positive labels to negative within one group, with no image altered, silently suppresses that group's disease detection. Across seven cohorts, three foundation-model encoders and four modalities, the backdoor installed once two thirds of that group's positive labels for one finding were flipped, 2.6% of the training set. Overall AUROC moved 0.004 and the comparison group stayed untouched. It cost 30.6 missed pleural effusions per 1,000 imaged patients of the targeted group and transferred to another health system. Harm reached patients whose race was never recorded, through the pixel shortcut rather than the chart entry, so an audit on recorded demographics is blind to 30% of studies. Five backdoor detectors failed. What works is auditing subgroup false-negative rate at the deployed threshold, which flagged 96% of installed failures compared to 73% for a rank-based audit.

title: Multi-view deep learning for classification of maxillary canine impaction severity using CBCT-derived images
abstract: Abstract Introduction. Accurate assessment of maxillary canine impaction is essential for timely orthodontic intervention. This study aimed to develop and evaluate a deep learning model using cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) derived images to classify maxillary canine impaction severity. Methods. This retrospective study included 148 maxillary canines from 74 patients, yielding 592 CBCT-derived images across four views (panoramic, frontal cephalogram, lateral cephalogram, and cross-sectional). Images were classified into normal eruption, mild impaction, and severe impaction based on orthodontist-defined radiographic criteria. A convolutional neural network (CNN), DenseNet-121, was fine-tuned and evaluated using five-fold cross-validation. Tooth-level predictions were obtained by combining per-view outputs, and performance was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Results. At the tooth level, the multi-view model achieved an overall accuracy of 91.2%, with a macro-averaged AUC of 0.94. Per-class sensitivity reached 93.4% (normal), 76.9% (mild), and 91.5% (severe); specificity exceeded 92% for all three classes. Conclusions. The proposed multi-view CNN model enables automated classification of maxillary canine impaction severity and demonstrates improved diagnostic performance with multi-view integration. This orthodontist-developed model may support early detection and multidisciplinary collaboration.

title: “Endoscopic Management of Advanced Juvenile Nasopharyngeal Angiofibroma with Extensive Infratemporal Fossa Extension: Surgical Challenges and Technical Modifications”- Case report
abstract: Abstract Background: Juvenile nasopharyngeal angiofibroma (JNA) is a rare, benign yet locally invasive vascular tumour affecting adolescent males. Advanced tumours extending into the infratemporal fossa (ITF) pose significant surgical challenges. Case Report: An 11-year-old boy presented with a one-year history of progressive left-sided proptosis and a two-month history of left cheek swelling. Imaging revealed a highly vascular mass centred in the left sphenopalatine fossa, extending into the infratemporal fossa, orbit, nasopharynx, cavernous sinus, and extradural temporal lobe. Preoperative embolisation was performed to reduce intraoperative blood loss. The tumour was completely excised via a transnasal endoscopic approach with few modifications. The postoperative course was uneventful, and follow-up imaging at two months demonstrated no residual disease. Histopathology confirmed JNA. Conclusion: This case demonstrates that exclusive endoscopic transnasal excision, combined with preoperative embolisation, can achieve complete resection of advanced JNA with extensive ITF extension, avoiding morbid open approaches.

title: Parents’ experiences of whole-body MRI-based surveillance for their child with genetic cancer risk: a longitudinal qualitative study
abstract: Abstract Broad genomic screening in pediatric oncology is increasingly identifying children with genetic cancer risk indicating intensive, lifelong surveillance. While this may improve early cancer detection, families face complex psychosocial challenges with unclear implications for adherence. We aimed to explore parents’ experiences of ongoing surveillance for their child with a multi-organ genetic cancer risk condition, including how these experiences changed over time. Parents’/caregivers’ of children (<18yrs) participating in WBMRI-based surveillance completed interviews at enrolment and following surveillance events. Interviews were transcribed and analyzed using reflexive thematic analysis. Thirteen parents (median age=41.4yrs; 54% female) of 13 children (median age=8.1yrs) participated in 33 interviews (median=2, range=1-5). Children had germline pathogenic/likely pathogenic variants in TP53 (n=10), BLM (n=2; biallelic), and RB1 (n=1) genes. Parents described surveillance as characterized by cyclical procedural and outcome-related uncertainty influenced by additional psychosocial stressors. Coping strategies evolved over time and involved emotional (e.g. compartmentalization) and practical strategies (e.g. simulating procedures). Administrative burdens, care co-ordination, and persistent fear of cancer occurrence remained significant challenges. Parents’ initially described children as focused on procedural aspects of surveillance, for some these perceptions shifted across repeated surveillance with some children showing increased cancer-related distress. A desire to benefit their child, seek reassurance, and contribute to research motivated ongoing engagement despite challenges. Parents perceive surveillance as worthwhile, despite emotional and practical burdens. Multidisciplinary care models that streamline communication and integrate proactive psychosocial and dedicated psychological support may reduce ongoing challenges.

title: Extranodal Rosai Dorfman Disease: An Unusual Course Without Nodal or Systemic Involvement- Case report
abstract: Abstract Introduction: Rosai–Dorfman disease (RDD) is a rare benign non-Langerhans cell histiocytic disorder that typically presents with painless cervical lymphadenopathy. Isolated extranodal disease involving the head and neck is uncommon, while recurrent multifocal disease without nodal or systemic involvement is exceptionally rare. We report a unique case of recurrent multifocal extranodal RDD confined to the sinonasal tract and eyelid. Case Report: A woman in her late 50s presented with recurrent nasal obstruction and epistaxis. Evaluation revealed a mass in the right nasal cavity, which was excised endoscopically. Histopathological examination established the diagnosis of extranodal RDD. During a 3-year follow-up, she experienced sequential recurrences involving the contralateral nasal cavity, nasal septum, anterior ethmoid sinus, and left lower eyelid. Each lesion was managed successfully with complete surgical excision, and histopathology consistently confirmed recurrent RDD. Despite multifocal recurrences, there was no evidence of cervical lymphadenopathy, systemic symptoms, or radiological features of aggressive disease. The patient remained symptom-free following each surgery and did not require systemic therapy. Conclusion This case highlights an unusual presentation of recurrent multifocal extranodal RDD involving the sinonasal tract and eyelid in the absence of nodal or systemic disease. Although recurrence is uncommon, RDD should be considered in the differential diagnosis of recurrent sinonasal masses. Histopathological confirmation remains essential for diagnosis, and complete surgical excision can provide excellent long-term disease control in patients with localized recurrent extranodal disease, avoiding the need for systemic treatment.

title: Hemorrhage-Induced Bias of [18F]FDG PET Signal Interpretation in Pancreatic Ductal Adenocarcinoma
abstract: Abstract Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is associated with high mortality and poor prognosis. Most patients present with unresectable PDAC, underscoring the need for reliable non-invasive imaging biomarkers. [ 18 F]fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography or[ 18 F]FDG PET provides metabolic information but lacks specificity for viable tumor tissue, as tracer uptake can be affected by inflammatory processes, potentially confounding tumor characterization or treatment-response assessment. This study explores the impact of hemorrhage and associated inflammatory changes on [ 18 F]FDG uptake in PDAC. Methods [ 18 F]FDG PET findings were correlated with MRI and histology in orthotopic PDAC models representing quasimesenchymal (PSN1) (n = 8; 4 hemorrhagic) and classical (HPAC) (n = 9; 6 hemorrhagic) subtypes in mice, and a clinical test cohort (n = 6; 4 hemorrhagic). Results In non-hemorrhagic murine tumors, [ 18 F]FDG PET reliably identified hypometabolic necrotic regions, allowing exclusion from analysis. In contrast, necrotic regions containing multifocal hemorrhage showed significantly higher [ 18 F]FDG uptake (HPAC SUV mean 1.42 ± 0.19 vs 1.10 ± 0.10, P = 0.036, PSN1 SUV mean 1.72 ± 0.15 vs 1.20 ± 0.14, P = 0.002). In patients, tumors with hemorrhage demonstrated higher SUV max than non-hemorrhagic tumors (7.57 ± 1.4 vs 3.41 ± 0.2). Reference-tissue normalization preserved these differences. Murine tumors exhibiting hemorrhage also showed increased macrophage infiltration. Conclusions Hemorrhage and associated inflammatory changes can confound [ 18 F]FDG PET interpretation, leading to overestimation of viable tumor tissue. Incorporating complementary structural imaging with careful region-of-interest definition improves the accuracy of [ 18 F]FDG PET-based PDAC characterization and treatment response assessment.

title: Extended Reality-Based Hepatic Surgical Planning: Impact on Task Time, Anatomic Accuracy, and Cognitive Burden in Novice Surgeons
abstract: Abstract Background : Traditional liver surgery education relies on 2D imaging and cadaveric specimens, causing misjudgments in complex 3D anatomy and hemodynamics, especially among junior surgeons. Objective : To develop LiverXR-Plan, a multimodal extended reality platform integrating structural imaging and hemodynamic simulation for education and surgical planning. Design : A prospective controlled trial compared LiverXR-Plan with 2D methods. Participants: 52 medical students and 47 residents. Interventions: Preoperative planning using 2D CT or LiverXR-Plan with 3D reconstruction and CFD simulation. Outcomes: Anatomical accuracy, completion time, and NASA-TLX workload. Results : Accuracy improved from 32.69% to 100% (students) and 74.47% to 100% (residents); time reduced by 54.40% and 51.12%. Hemodynamic visualization enabled risk prediction; workload significantly decreased. Conclusions : LiverXR-Plan enhances surgical planning competency and shifts liver surgery education from experience-dependent to data-driven decision-making.

title: Clinical Characteristics, Microbiological Profile, and Antimicrobial Resistance of Pseudomonas aeruginosa in Hospitalized Patients with Bronchiectasis: A 10-Year Single- Center Cohort Study
abstract: Abstract Background. Pseudomonas aeruginosa (PA) is the most clinically significant respiratory pathogen in patients with bronchiectasis, yet data from mainland China on PA colonization, antimicrobial resistance, and its impact on hospitalization outcomes remain limited. We aimed to characterize the clinical and microbiological profile of PA among hospitalized patients with bronchiectasis over a 10-year period. Methods. We conducted a retrospective cohort study of all adult patients hospitalized with a primary diagnosis of bronchiectasis at Beijing Chaoyang Hospital, a tertiary referral respiratory center in China, between January 2014 and December 2024. Clinical, radiological, laboratory, and microbiological data were extracted from the electronic hospital information system. Respiratory samples were cultured using standard microbiological methods; antimicrobial susceptibility testing was performed by the clinical microbiology laboratory. Patients were classified as PA-positive or PA-negative on the basis of respiratory culture results. Comparisons between groups used the Mann-Whitney U test for continuous variables and the chi-square test for categorical variables. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with PA colonization. Results. Among 7787 hospital admissions from 2,503 unique patients (mean age 59.9 ± 13.4 years; 56.4% female), 942 admissions (29.2%) underwent respiratory culture. PA was the dominant pathogen, isolated in 338 of 942 cultured admissions (35.9%), followed by Klebsiella pneumoniae (3.0%), Acinetobacter baumannii (2.4%), and Aspergillus spp. (6.2%). PA-positive admissions were younger (median 60 vs. 64 years), had longer hospitalization (12 vs. 11 days), higher white blood cell counts (7.28 vs. 6.56 × 10⁹/L), higher platelet counts, and higher PaCO2 (51 vs. 44 mmHg) than PA-negative admissions (all p < 0.05). In multivariable analysis, CT-documented bronchiectasis (adjusted OR 1.64, 95% CI 1.19–2.24) and higher WBC count (adjusted OR 1.06 per unit, 95% CI 1.02–1.10) were independently associated with PA colonization, whereas older age was protective (adjusted OR 0.98, 95% CI 0.97–0.99). Among 821 PA isolates with comprehensive susceptibility testing, 20.0% were multidrug-resistant, 26.4% were carbapenem-resistant, and 25.0% were fluoroquinolone-resistant; amikacin and tobramycin retained the highest susceptibility rates (90.4% and 93.8%, respectively). CT-documented bronchiectasis was also the strongest predictor of recurrent hospitalization (adjusted OR 3.17, 95% CI 2.46–4.07). Conclusions. PA is the predominant respiratory pathogen among hospitalized patients with bronchiectasis in Beijing, associated with more extensive structural lung disease, higher systemic inflammation, worse ventilatory function, and prolonged hospitalization. title: Fourth ventricular cerebral sparganosis mimicking ependymoma with obstructive hydrocephalus: a case report
abstract: Abstract Background Cerebral sparganosis is a rare parasitic infection of the central nervous system that usually involves the cerebral parenchyma and may show migratory or tunnel-like imaging features. Direct ventricular involvement is uncommon, and a fourth ventricular mass-forming presentation can closely resemble an intraventricular neoplasm. Case presentation: A 48-year-old man from Yunnan Province, China, presented with more than 5 months of dizziness and headache and two syncopal episodes. Magnetic resonance imaging showed a 2.9 × 2.1 × 3.7 cm rounded lesion centered in the fourth ventricle with focal nodular enhancement and mild supratentorial hydrocephalus. Peripheral eosinophil counts were normal. Ependymoma was considered the leading preoperative diagnosis. Microsurgical resection through a midline suboccipital approach revealed a cystic lesion containing a yellowish nodular cord-like structure. Histopathological examination demonstrated parasitic tegument-like and parenchymal structures with surrounding inflammatory-cell infiltration, consistent with sparganosis. Postoperatively, the patient received praziquantel and supportive therapy. Headache and dizziness resolved, and no recurrence was identified during 5 months of follow-up. Conclusions Fourth ventricular cerebral sparganosis may lack classic parenchymal imaging features and mimic ependymoma. In patients from endemic regions or with relevant exposure, sparganosis should remain in the differential diagnosis of atypical fourth ventricular cystic or nodular enhancing lesions even when peripheral eosinophilia is absent. Intraoperative recognition and histopathological examination can be decisive when preoperative testing is inconclusive.

title: Lightweight Deep Learning for Processing 3D Medical Images: A Systematic Review
abstract: Abstract Deep learning for three dimension (3D) modalities such as CT, MRI, and PET offers promise to improve diagnostic accuracy, surgical planning, and visualization of disease progression, as 3D image data provide high resolution volumetric representation. However, 3D deep learning models are computationally heavy and demand powerful hardware that is not always available or affordable, restrictingtheir use in resource-constrained settings such as rural clinics, edge devices, and low- and middle-income countries. Hence, there is a growing interest in building lightweight deep learning models, in general, and for 3D imaging, in particular. This article systematically and critically reviews lightweight deep learning for processing 3D medical images, examining model compression techniques such as knowledge distillation, quantization, pruning and efficient architectural designs, together with the datasets, tools, and deployment environments involved. These techniques substantially reduce parameters, memory, and inference time with modest accuracy loss. We also identify several research gaps in these approaches, such as the accuracy mismatch between lightweight and standard models, difficulty handling small anatomical structures while keeping models compact, limited testing on real resource-constrained hardware, weak integration of clinical information, and the absence of efficiency-aware evaluation metrics. We outline future directions, cluding robust lightweight designs, purpose-built compact 3D datasets, standardized efficiency metrics, and lightweight multimodal models.

title: Giant Partially Thrombosed Ophthalmic Segment Internal Carotid Artery Aneurysm With Severe Angiographic–Radiological Discordance: Implications for Microsurgical Strategy
abstract: Abstract Background Giant partially thrombosed aneurysms of the ophthalmic segment of the internal carotid artery (ICA) present substantial diagnostic and therapeutic challenges because intraluminal thrombus and mural calcification can obscure the true aneurysm morphology, leading to underestimation of lesion size on angiography. Methods A 53-year-old man with progressive headache without focal neurological deficits or objective visual impairment underwent multimodal imaging including CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA. The imaging findings were integrated for operative planning, and microsurgical clipping with staged thrombectomy was performed. Results CT and MRI revealed a giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysm compressing the optic apparatus, whereas DSA depicted only a small residual lumen, demonstrating marked angiographic–radiological discordance. Microsurgical clip reconstruction with staged intraluminal thrombectomy achieved complete aneurysm exclusion with preservation of the parent ICA and ophthalmic artery. The patient recovered without new neurological deficits and remained functionally independent at 6-month follow-up. Conclusions Giant partially thrombosed ophthalmic segment ICA aneurysms may be substantially underestimated by DSA alone. Integration of CT, MRI, CTA, and DSA is critical for defining true aneurysm morphology and optimizing skull base microsurgical strategy. Microsurgical reconstruction with staged thrombectomy remains a definitive treatment option in selected patients.

title: Multimodal Study of Brain Structural Alterations, Functional Gradient Perturbations, and Transcriptomic Specialization in Trigeminal Neuralgia Using 5.0 Tesla MRI
abstract: Abstract Objective: This study aimed to harness the superior imaging capability of 5.0 T MRI to comprehensively characterize structural brain alterations, functional connectome gradient perturbations, and their underlying transcriptomic correlates in patients with trigeminal neuralgia (TN). By constructing an interpretative framework linking macroscopic gradient changes to microscale gene specialization. Methods: Thirty‑five TN patients and sixty‑four healthy controls (HC) were enrolled. All participants underwent 3D high‑resolution T1 and resting‑state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) on a 5.0 T scanner. Functional connectome gradients were derived from the functional connectivity (FC) matrix via diffusion map embedding. Gray matter volume (GMV) was computed using voxel‑based morphometry (VBM), and structure‑function coupling was assessed via spatial correlations. Partial least squares (PLS) regression was employed to identify gene sets associated with gradient perturbations, followed by enrichment analysis to reveal the underlying biological processes. Results: TN patients exhibited attenuated extreme values and increased intermediate values on the primary gradient, with altered gradient scores across multiple networks, indicative of a global gradient compression. GMV reductions was observed in the medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and superior frontal gyrus (SFG), while gradient scores were decreased in the mPFC and ventral anterior cingulate cortex (vACC). Spatial correlation analyses revealed structure‑function decoupling in the sensorimotor (SMN), limbic (LIB), and frontoparietal (FPN) networks. Transcriptomic analyses showed that cortical gradient perturbations were strongly associated with genes involved in voltage‑gated ion channels, membrane potential regulation, and neurotransmitter release. Significant enrichment of sodium channel, Na⁺/K⁺‑ATPase, and GABA receptor genes further corroborated the ion channelopathy basis of TN. Conclusion: 5.0T MRI-based connectome gradient analysis reveals global compression and network-specific reorganization in TN. mPFC/vACC dedifferentiation reflects hierarchical collapse of descending pain inhibition, underpinning chronification. Gene enrichment corroborates ion channelopathy and suggests novel targets. This multi-scale framework integrates structure, function, and transcriptomics to advance mechanistic insights.

title: Development and Internal Validation of a Prediction Model for Ureteral Access Sheath Insertion Depth During Flexible Ureteroscopy Based on Patient Anthropometric and Anatomical Parameters
abstract: Abstract Backgound:Optimal placement of UAS during fURS) relies largely on surgeon experience. Insertion that is too deep may cause ureteral injury, whereas insertion that is too shallow necessitates repeated fluoroscopic adjustment. This study aimed to develop and internally validate a machine learning model that predicts UAS insertion depth using the L1 vertebra–pubic symphysis distance and readily available anthropometric parameters. Methods This single-center cohort study enrolled 124 consecutive patients who underwent fURS with UAS placement between April 2025 and July 2026. The L1–pubic symphysis distance was measured on preoperative plain radiographs or CT scout images. Candidate predictors included height, age, sex, side, BMI and the L1–pubic symphysis distance. The outcome was the actual UAS insertion depth (cm), measured intraoperatively from the perineal skin to the ureteropelvic junction. The dataset was divided into training (70%, n = 86) and test (30%, n = 38) sets using stratified random sampling by sex. Six regression algorithms were compared, including Ridge regression, least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (Lasso), Bayesian ridge, random forest, support vector regression, and multilayer perceptron. Hyperparameters were tuned by five-fold cross-validation. Model performance was assessed using R², mean absolute error (MAE), root mean square error (RMSE), and the proportion of predictions within ± 2 cm of the actual depth. The final model was refitted on the entire cohort, and bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were obtained for all coefficients. The study followed the Transparent Reporting of a multivariable prediction model for Individual Prognosis Or Diagnosis (TRIPOD) guideline. Results The mean UAS insertion depth was 33.7 ± 2.8 cm (range, 26.5–40.0 cm). Height (r = 0.749), male sex (r = 0.661), L1–pubic symphysis distance (r = 0.563), BMI (r = 0.251), and younger age (r = − 0.498) were correlated with insertion depth. Ridge regression with regularization parameter α = 10 achieved the best balance of accuracy and interpretability, with a test-set R² of 0.661, MAE of 1.24 cm, RMSE of 1.56 cm, and 78.9% of predictions falling within ± 2 cm. Five-fold cross-validation yielded an R² of 0.642 ± 0.067. Leave-one-out cross-validation across all 124 patients produced an R² of 0.649, MAE of 1.39 cm, and 77.4% accuracy within ± 2 cm, substantially outperforming an L1-distance-only model (R² = 0.291; MAE = 1.86 cm). Bootstrap internal validation (1,000 resamples) confirmed minimal overfitting (optimism = 0.026), with an optimism-corrected R² of 0.659, MAE of 1.39 cm, and a calibration slope of 1.033. Standardized coefficients identified male sex (β = 0.927; 95% CI, 0.651–1.205), height (β = 0.811; 95% CI, 0.444–1.148), and L1–pubic symphysis distance (β = 0.740; 95% CI, 0.396–1.086) as the strongest predictors, with BMI also contributing independently (β = 0.410; 95% CI, 0.164–0.674). A freely accessible online calculator was developed for clinical use. Conclusion A multivariable Ridge regression model incorporating the L1–pubic symphysis distance and anthropometric parameters can predict UAS insertion depth with clinically acceptable accuracy. The novel L1–pubic symphysis radiographic measurement, obtainable from routine preoperative imaging without additional examination, contributes independently to depth prediction. External validation in larger and more diverse cohorts is warranted before broad clinical implementation.

title: A Systematic Comparative Literature Review of Biomarkers, Imaging, and Therapeutic Strategies for Endometrial Cancer: Toward an Estrogen Receptor-Guided Near-Infrared Fluorescence Imaging and Endocrine Therapy Pipeline
abstract: Abstract Endometrial cancer (EC) is the most common gynecologic malignancy in high-income countries, with incidence rising alongside increasing obesity and population aging. Diagnosis still depends on invasive tissue biopsy and histopathology, a pathway that is costly, time-consuming, and burdensome for patients. As precision medicine increasingly emphasizes biomarker-guided, minimally invasive strategies, this study systematically compares candidate biomarkers, imaging modalities, and therapeutic strategies to identify the most clinically suitable combination for a minimally invasive diagnostic-therapeutic pipeline for EC. A systematic comparative literature analysis was conducted using PubMed, Google Scholar, Web of Science, ClinicalTrials.gov, and FDA resources, restricted to English-language publications from 2013–2026. Evidence on prevalence, diagnostic accuracy, safety, cost, and therapeutic relevance was organized into weighted decision matrices and a Multi-Criteria Decision Analysis. Among five candidate biomarkers, the estrogen receptor (ER) scored highest, reflecting its high prevalence in Type I endometrioid tumors, established assay infrastructure, and direct actionability with endocrine therapy. Among four imaging modalities, near-infrared (NIR) fluorescence endoscopy scored highest based on real-time signal acquisition and compatibility with existing endoscopic infrastructure. Endocrine therapy showed the strongest compatibility with ER-positive disease. Integrating these findings produced a proposed same-day pipeline, ER-targeted NIR fluorescence detection followed by endocrine therapy initiation, with an estimated reduction in time-to-treatment from 10–15 days to under 48 hours. This pipeline offers a scientifically coherent alternative to the conventional biopsy-dependent pathway for Type I, hormone-receptor-positive disease. However, this synthesis is based entirely on published literature; prospective validation, including probe development, imaging accuracy studies, and clinical trials, is required before real-world implementation.

title: MOM-PD: Multimodal Biomarker Optimization for Parkinson's Disease Machine learning-assisted multimodal detection and clinical staging
abstract: Abstract Background: Parkinson's disease (PD) diagnosis relies primarily on clinical motor examination, and the prodromal phase preceding overt motor manifestations remains difficult to identify. No single biomarker modality has been shown to be both sensitive and specific across the full disease spectrum, and how best to integrate multimodal data for stage-specific detection is unclear. Objective: To optimize a multimodal biomarker framework using machine learning based on Parkinson's Progression Markers Initiative (PPMI) data, and to define stage-specific biomarkerpanels for manifest PD detection, prodromal identification, and longitudinal progression monitoring. Methods: We analyzed 948 PPMI participants (445 PD, 389 prodromal, 111 healthy controls [HC], 3 SWEDD) with 18 candidate biomarkers spanning dopamine transporter SPECT (DaTscanSBR), structural MRI (FreeSurfer 7 cortical and subcortical metrics), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and MDS-UPDRS Parts I–IV. Feature-wide association analysis with Mann-Whitney U tests and Cohen's d was followed by random forest Gini importance ranking. Random forest classifiers (500 trees, 5-fold stratified cross-validation) were trained on three feature sets: (1) DaTscan + clinical; (2) structural MRI only; (3) full multimodal combination. Four-year longitudinal trajectories (BL, V06, V10) of motor scores and grey matter volume were characterized. Results: For PD vs HC, the DaTscan-clinical model achieved near-perfect discrimination (AUC = 0.999, 95% CI 0.997–1.000), far exceeding structural MRI alone (AUC = 0.526). Top discriminative features were putaminal SBR, striatal SBR, and MDS-UPDRS Part III motor score. Prodromal vs HC discrimination was more challenging (AUC = 0.700), with subcortical grey matteratrophy as the leading signal while DaTscan SBR was non-discriminative (P = 0.43). PD vs prodromal classification was excellent (AUC = 0.984). Longitudinally, PD motor scores increased ~1.5 points/year and grey matter volume declined ~0.85%/year. Conclusions: Multimodal biomarkers display staging-dependent complementarity: DaTscan and motor scales dominate manifest PD identification, while subcortical volumetric MRI enablesprodromal detection. Stage-tailored biomarker panels support improved PD phenotyping and early screening for clinical trial enrichment.

title: CAM-Threshold-Guided Weakly Supervised Lesion Segmentation and Relative Lesion-Burden Stratification of Wheat Stripe Rust Using CF2- WRD and Light-UNet
abstract: Abstract Accurate localization and quantification of wheat stripe rust lesions are important for phenotyping and disease management, yet dense pixel-level annotation is costly. We present a Grad-CAM-guided weakly supervised framework that reuses a dual-branch image classifier, CF2-WRD, to generate pseudo-labels for a compact Light-UNet segmenter. The dataset contained 34,694 images in 87 image-level categories, split into 27,834 training, 3,430 validation, and 3,430 test images. CF2-WRD achieved validation and test accuracies of 0.8776 and 0.8711. Among four CAM thresholds, 0.40 produced the highest agreement with CAM-derived validation pseudo-labels (mIoU 0.6584, Dice 0.7101, lesion IoU 0.5555), whereas 0.45 was used as a conservative operating point. Raising the segmentation probability threshold from 0.50 to 0.80 reduced mean predicted lesion-to-leaf ratio from 55.02% to 29.63% in a 300-image subset. The 3,430-image burden distribution was stratified by empirical quartiles. Because no independent manual lesion masks or expert-calibrated severity labels were available, overlap metrics quantify agreement with weak-supervision targets and burden groups represent dataset-relative rankings rather than agronomic severity grades.

We present a Grad-CAM-guided weakly supervised framework that reuses a dual-branch image classifier, CF2-WRD, to generate pseudo-labels for a compact Light-UNet segmenter. The dataset contained 34,694 images in 87 image-level categories, split into 27,834 training, 3,430 validation, and 3,430 test images. CF2-WRD achieved validation and test accuracies of 0.8776 and 0.8711.
